Unit One · The Case for the Story
Sehemu ya Kwanza · Hoja ya Kutetea Simulizi
Why Story? The Biblical Case for Narrative Preaching
Kwa Nini Simulizi? Hoja ya Kibiblia ya Kuhubiri kwa Masimulizi

All evangelical preachers are concerned to make the sermon biblical. Many conclude that the only legitimate form is the expository message — and too often it arrives loaded with explanation and as dry as Ezekiel's bones. But consider the preaching of Jesus. It would be hard to say He was not preaching the Word of God; yet He did not preach expository messages. He mostly told stories.

Wahubiri wote wa Kiinjili wanajali kwamba mahubiri yawe ya Kibiblia. Wengi huhitimisha kwamba muundo pekee halali ni mahubiri ya kifafanuzi — na mara nyingi mno huja yakiwa yamejaa maelezo na makavu kama mifupa ya Ezekieli. Lakini tafakari mahubiri ya Yesu. Itakuwa vigumu kusema kwamba Yeye hakuwa akihubiri Neno la Mungu; hata hivyo hakuhubiri mahubiri ya kifafanuzi. Mara nyingi alisimulia hadithi.
1.1 The Preacher's Anxiety About Stories
1.1 Wasiwasi wa Mhubiri Kuhusu Hadithi

There has always been a question whether storytelling is valid for the preacher. On one side, people listen and are moved — but they are also entertained, and we worry that an entertained congregation is not a fed one. On the other side, storytelling is not expository preaching, and we fear the story has no "meat." Some treat the illustration as mere filler, a sugar coating around the real medicine of the sermon. What are we to do? Before we can build a story sermon, we have to settle this question of conscience, because a preacher who secretly believes stories are a compromise will never tell one well.

Daima kumekuwa na swali kama kusimulia hadithi ni halali kwa mhubiri. Upande mmoja, watu husikiliza na kuguswa — lakini pia hufurahishwa tu, nasi tunahofu kwamba kusanyiko lililofurahishwa si kusanyiko lililolishwa. Upande mwingine, kusimulia hadithi si kuhubiri kwa kifafanuzi, nasi tunaogopa kwamba hadithi haina "nyama." Wengine huchukulia kielelezo kuwa kijazo tu, utamu wa sukari unaozunguka dawa halisi ya mahubiri. Tufanye nini basi? Kabla hatujajenga mahubiri ya simulizi, ni lazima tulitatue swali hili la dhamiri, kwa sababu mhubiri anayeamini kwa siri kwamba hadithi ni maafikiano ya kupunguza ukweli hataweza kamwe kusimulia moja vizuri.

This is not a new debate. Ever since the church had pulpits, earnest men have worried that a sermon full of stories is a sermon empty of substance, and the worry is not foolish — we will spend a whole later unit on the real dangers it points to. But a danger that can be abused is not the same as a method that must be avoided. Fire can burn the house or warm it; the answer is not to forbid fire but to learn to handle it. So it is with the story. The question before us is not whether stories can be misused — anything can — but whether, rightly used, the story is a fit vessel for the Word of God. To that question the practice of the Lord Jesus returns a thunderous yes.

Huu si mjadala mpya. Tangu kanisa lilipokuwa na mimbari, watu wenye bidii wamehofu kwamba mahubiri yaliyojaa hadithi ni mahubiri yasiyo na kiini, na hofu hiyo si ya kipumbavu — tutatumia sehemu nzima baadaye kuchunguza hatari halisi inazozionyesha. Lakini hatari inayoweza kutumiwa vibaya si sawa na mbinu inayopaswa kuepukwa. Moto unaweza kuiteketeza nyumba au kuipasha joto; jibu si kuukataza moto bali kujifunza kuushughulikia. Ndivyo ilivyo kwa simulizi. Swali lililo mbele yetu si kama hadithi zinaweza kutumiwa vibaya — kitu chochote kinaweza — bali kama, ikitumiwa ipasavyo, simulizi ni chombo kinachofaa kwa Neno la Mungu. Kwa swali hilo, desturi ya Bwana Yesu inajibu "ndiyo" kwa sauti kama ya radi.
This whole course is the long answer. But it rests on two short ideas, and if you grasp them, everything else follows. Let us state them plainly and then unfold them.
Kozi hii yote ni jibu refu. Lakini inasimama juu ya mawazo mawili mafupi, na ukiyashika, mengine yote yanafuata. Hebu tuyaeleze waziwazi kisha tuyafunue.
1.2 First Idea: The Story Does Not Contain the Message — the Story IS the Message
1.2 Wazo la Kwanza: Simulizi Haibebi Ujumbe Tu — Simulizi NDIYO Ujumbe

The objection that stories are "only entertainment" must be answered first, and it is answered by the practice of Jesus. While our Lord sometimes preached in a more direct way, He characteristically told stories. The Gospel writers tell us that "the common people heard him gladly" (Mark 12:37) and that "he did not say anything to them without using a parable" (Matthew 13:34). His stories were about people and situations His audience could see themselves inside. The story was not a sideline to the message; it was the message of God, gripping and relevant. The illustration we are tempted to call filler is, in fact, the vehicle that carries the truth into the heart.

Pingamizi kwamba hadithi ni "burudani tu" lazima lijibiwe kwanza, nalo linajibiwa na desturi ya Yesu. Ingawa Bwana wetu wakati mwingine alihubiri kwa njia ya moja kwa moja zaidi, kwa kawaida alisimulia hadithi. Waandishi wa Injili wanatuambia kwamba "mkutano mkubwa wakamsikiliza kwa furaha" (Marko 12:37) na kwamba "pasipo mfano hakuwaambia neno" (Mathayo 13:34). Hadithi zake zilihusu watu na hali ambazo wasikilizaji wake waliweza kujiona wakiwa ndani yake. Simulizi haikuwa jambo la pembeni la ujumbe; ilikuwa ujumbe wa Mungu, wenye kuvutia na unaohusika na maisha. Kielelezo tunachoshawishika kukiita kijazo, kwa kweli, ni chombo kinachobeba ukweli hadi moyoni.

Look at Luke 15. Jesus is, in effect, asked the question, "What is God like?" He does not answer with three points about lostness. He tells three stories — the lost sheep, the lost coin, and the lost son. All three make the same point: God is a seeker who will not rest until the lost is found. Jesus could have given a lecture on the doctrine of divine grace. Instead He gave us a shepherd crossing the hills, a woman lighting a lamp, and a father running down a road. If we examine the preaching of Jesus honestly, we conclude that He was utterly committed to conveying the truth of God — and that He chiefly did it through stories. The story was not how He decorated the message. The story was how He delivered it.

Tazama Luka 15. Kwa maana fulani Yesu anaulizwa swali, "Mungu yukoje?" Hajibu kwa hoja tatu kuhusu kupotea. Anasimulia hadithi tatu — kondoo aliyepotea, shilingi iliyopotea, na mwana aliyepotea. Zote tatu zinasisitiza jambo moja: Mungu ni mtafutaji ambaye hatapumzika mpaka kilichopotea kipatikane. Yesu angeweza kutoa hotuba juu ya fundisho la neema ya Mungu. Badala yake alitupa mchungaji akivuka vilima, mwanamke akiwasha taa, na baba akikimbia barabarani. Tukichunguza mahubiri ya Yesu kwa uaminifu, tunahitimisha kwamba alijitoa kikamilifu kuwasilisha ukweli wa Mungu — na kwamba alifanya hivyo hasa kwa njia ya hadithi. Simulizi haikuwa namna alivyoupamba ujumbe. Simulizi ilikuwa namna alivyouwasilisha.

Nor was Jesus the first. The prophets before Him reached for the story whenever the plain word had failed. When Isaiah wanted to expose a nation's ingratitude, he sang them a love song about a vineyard that yielded only wild grapes, and the people leaned in to enjoy the song before they realized it was about them (Isaiah 5:1–7). When Jotham wanted to rebuke the men of Shechem, he told them a fable about trees that went out to anoint a king (Judges 9:7–15). Ezekiel was commanded by God Himself to put the message in riddles and parables (Ezekiel 17:2). And from Genesis to Revelation, the largest part of the Bible is neither law nor doctrine nor epistle but narrative — story is the very form in which God chose to give the greater part of His own Word. The preacher who fills his mouth with story is not departing from the Scriptures; he is imitating them.

Wala Yesu hakuwa wa kwanza. Manabii waliomtangulia walichukua simulizi kila mara neno la wazi liliposhindwa. Isaya alipotaka kufichua kutokushukuru kwa taifa, aliwaimbia wimbo wa mapenzi kuhusu shamba la mizabibu lililozaa zabibu-mwitu tu, na watu walisogea karibu kuufurahia wimbo kabla hawajatambua kwamba ulikuwa unawahusu wao (Isaya 5:1–7). Yothamu alipotaka kuwakemea watu wa Shekemu, aliwasimulia hekaya ya miti iliyokwenda kumtia mafuta mfalme (Waamuzi 9:7–15). Ezekieli aliamriwa na Mungu Mwenyewe kuuweka ujumbe katika vitendawili na mifano (Ezekieli 17:2). Na tangu Mwanzo hadi Ufunuo, sehemu kubwa zaidi ya Biblia si sheria wala mafundisho wala nyaraka bali masimulizi — simulizi ndiyo muundo hasa ambao Mungu aliuchagua kutoa sehemu kubwa ya Neno lake Mwenyewe. Mhubiri anayejaza kinywa chake masimulizi haachi Maandiko; anayaiga.
1.3 Second Idea: The Facts May Convince the Mind, but a Story Moves the Heart
1.3 Wazo la Pili: Ukweli Halisi Unaweza Kushawishi Akili, Lakini Simulizi Huugusa Moyo

The Lord sent the prophet Nathan to King David after David had committed adultery, murder, and the long lie that covered them (2 Samuel 12:1–7). David was trying to hide his sin, and David held absolute power — he could have put the poor preacher to death with a word. So Nathan did not begin with the charge. He told a story: a rich man with many flocks, and a poor man with a single pet ewe lamb that ate from his plate and slept in his arms; and when a traveler came, the rich man spared his own flocks and took the poor man's lamb. David's anger blazed against the man in the story — and only then did Nathan say, "Thou art the man." In the picture, Bathsheba is the beautiful ewe lamb, David is the rich man with many sheep, and Uriah is the poor man who had only one. It was not enough to tell David the facts; he already knew the facts. He had to be persuaded through the heart.

BWANA alimtuma nabii Nathani kwa Mfalme Daudi baada ya Daudi kufanya uzinzi, uuaji, na uongo wa muda mrefu uliovifunika (2 Samweli 12:1–7). Daudi alikuwa akijaribu kuficha dhambi yake, na Daudi alikuwa na mamlaka kamili — angeweza kumwua mhubiri yule maskini kwa neno moja tu. Kwa hiyo Nathani hakuanza na shtaka. Alisimulia hadithi: tajiri mwenye makundi mengi, na maskini mwenye mwana-kondoo jike mmoja tu aliyempenda, aliyekula katika sahani yake na kulala kifuani mwake; na msafiri alipofika, tajiri aliyahurumia makundi yake mwenyewe akamtwaa mwana-kondoo wa yule maskini. Hasira ya Daudi iliwaka juu ya mtu yule wa hadithi — na hapo tu ndipo Nathani aliposema, "Wewe ndiwe mtu huyo." Katika picha hiyo, Bathsheba ndiye mwana-kondoo jike mzuri, Daudi ndiye tajiri mwenye kondoo wengi, na Uria ndiye maskini aliyekuwa na mmoja tu. Haikutosha kumwambia Daudi ukweli halisi; alikuwa tayari anaujua ukweli huo. Ilibidi ashawishiwe kupitia moyo.

What Nathan did has a name. Warren Wiersbe borrows the word "connecting" from the field of psychotherapy to describe what happens when you put together things that previously seemed unrelated, so that the hearer gains a new insight into his own life (Preaching and Teaching with Imagination). The preacher cannot be a mere channel pouring information from his mind into the minds of his listeners; he must connect with them, and the story is the surest way to do it. Hal Luccock put it memorably: "The purpose of preaching is not to make people see reasons, but visions" (In the Minister's Workshop). Reasons inform the mind; visions move the whole person to act. The story does not abandon the truth — it carries the truth past the guarded gate of the intellect and sets it down in the heart, where decisions are actually made.

Alichofanya Nathani kina jina. Warren Wiersbe anaazima neno "kuunganisha" (connecting) kutoka katika fani ya tiba ya nafsi (psychotherapy) kueleza kinachotokea unapoweka pamoja mambo ambayo hapo awali yalionekana hayahusiani, ili msikilizaji apate ufahamu mpya kuhusu maisha yake mwenyewe (Preaching and Teaching with Imagination). Mhubiri hawezi kuwa mfereji tu unaomimina habari kutoka akilini mwake kwenda akilini mwa wasikilizaji wake; lazima aungane nao, na simulizi ndiyo njia ya uhakika zaidi ya kufanya hivyo. Hal Luccock aliliweka jambo hili kwa namna isiyosahaulika: "Kusudi la kuhubiri si kuwafanya watu waone sababu, bali maono" (In the Minister's Workshop). Sababu huiarifu akili; maono huusukuma utu mzima kutenda. Simulizi haiuachi ukweli — inaubeba ukweli kupita lango linalolindwa la akili na kuuweka moyoni, mahali ambapo maamuzi hufanywa kwa kweli.

Scripture locates our deepest decisions not in the head but in the heart. As a man thinks in his heart, so is he (Proverbs 23:7); out of the heart are the issues of life (Proverbs 4:23); and it is with the heart, Paul says, that man believes unto righteousness (Romans 10:10). A truth that reaches only the mind has stopped on the doorstep of the house; it has not yet entered the room where the man actually lives. This is why the bare statement of a fact so often changes nothing. David already possessed every fact of his guilt; what he lacked was a way to feel it as his own — and the story gave him that in a single sentence. The preacher who only informs is leaving his hearers exactly where the prophet refused to leave the king.

Maandiko yanaweka maamuzi yetu ya ndani kabisa si kichwani bali moyoni. Kama mtu aonavyo nafsini mwake, ndivyo alivyo (Mithali 23:7); moyoni ndiko zitokako chemchemi za uzima (Mithali 4:23); na ni kwa moyo, Paulo asema, mtu huamini hata kupata haki (Warumi 10:10). Ukweli unaofikia akili tu umesimama kizingitini mwa nyumba; bado haujaingia katika chumba ambamo mtu huyo anaishi kwa kweli. Ndiyo sababu kutamka tu jambo la kweli mara nyingi hakubadilishi chochote. Daudi tayari alikuwa na kila ukweli kuhusu hatia yake; alichokosa ni njia ya kuuhisi kuwa wake mwenyewe — na simulizi ilimpa hilo kwa sentensi moja. Mhubiri anayearifu tu anawaacha wasikilizaji wake mahali pale pale ambapo nabii alikataa kumwacha mfalme.
1.4 What the Research Confirms
1.4 Kile Ambacho Utafiti Unathibitisha

This is not only a theological observation; it is a measurable one. Rudolph Flesch studied what makes writing interesting and identified two factors above the rest. The first is the use of personal words — I, we, you, and personal names like Sally, Fred, or Mr. Johnson. The second is the telling of personal stories (cited in Nash, The Christian Communicator's Handbook). The plainest way to say it is this: people like stories about people. The abstract noun glances off the mind; the named person walks straight into the imagination.

Hili si tu jambo la kitheolojia lililoonekana; ni jambo linaloweza kupimwa. Rudolph Flesch alichunguza kinachofanya maandishi yavutie na akabainisha mambo mawili kuliko mengine yote. La kwanza ni matumizi ya maneno ya kibinafsi — mimi, sisi, wewe, na majina ya watu kama Sally, Fred, au Bwana Johnson. La pili ni kusimulia hadithi za kibinafsi (imenukuliwa katika Nash, The Christian Communicator's Handbook). Njia rahisi kabisa ya kulisema ni hii: watu hupenda hadithi kuhusu watu. Nomino dhahania huiteleza akili; mtu mwenye jina huingia moja kwa moja katika fikira.

I once had the opportunity to bring a guest preacher to our church. He was widely known as a dull preacher, and I confess I was anxious. Then I had an inspiration: I asked him simply to tell his testimony. He stood up and spoke, and he was animated and interesting — the same man. I have since heard him attempt a traditional sermon, and almost everyone's eyes glazed over. What was the difference? It was the power of the story. Nothing about the man changed; only the form of his message changed, and the form made all the difference.

Wakati mmoja nilipata nafasi ya kumleta mhubiri mgeni kanisani kwetu. Alijulikana sana kama mhubiri anayechosha, nami nakiri nilikuwa na wasiwasi. Kisha nikapata wazo: nilimwomba asimulie tu ushuhuda wake. Alisimama akaongea, naye alikuwa mchangamfu na mwenye kuvutia — mtu yule yule. Tangu hapo nimemsikia akijaribu kuhubiri mahubiri ya kawaida, na karibu macho ya kila mtu yalipoteza hamu. Tofauti ilikuwa nini? Ilikuwa nguvu ya simulizi. Hakuna kilichobadilika kwa mtu huyo; ni muundo wa ujumbe wake tu uliobadilika, na muundo huo ulileta tofauti yote.

Ask the average churchgoer on Monday what last Sunday's sermon was about, and he will rarely give you the proposition or the points. He will tell you the story the preacher told. The illustration is not what he forgot on the way to the truth; very often it is the one thing he carried home, and the truth came home riding inside it. This is not a failure in the hearer to be corrected but a feature of the human soul to be used. We were made to remember in pictures and to be moved by persons, and the wise preacher works with the grain of the people God actually made rather than against it.

Muulize mshiriki wa kawaida wa kanisa siku ya Jumatatu mahubiri ya Jumapili iliyopita yalihusu nini, naye mara chache atakupa wazo kuu au hoja. Atakuambia hadithi aliyoisimulia mhubiri. Kielelezo si kile alichokisahau akiwa njiani kuelekea ukweli; mara nyingi sana ndicho kitu kimoja alichokibeba hadi nyumbani, na ukweli ukafika nyumbani ukiwa umepanda ndani yake. Huu si udhaifu wa msikilizaji unaopaswa kurekebishwa bali ni tabia ya nafsi ya mwanadamu inayopaswa kutumiwa. Tuliumbwa kukumbuka kwa picha na kuguswa na watu, na mhubiri mwenye hekima hufanya kazi akipatana na jinsi Mungu alivyowaumba watu kwa kweli, badala ya kwenda kinyume na hali hiyo.
1.5 Jesus the Master Storyteller — and Our Mandate
1.5 Yesu Msimulizi Mkuu — na Agizo Letu

So we return to where we began. Jesus is the Master Storyteller, and He is the model by which every preacher is measured. If the Son of God characteristically carried the deepest truths of heaven on the back of a story about a farmer, a coin, or a wayward boy, then the preacher who despises the story has set himself above his Lord. Narrative preaching is not a betrayal of biblical preaching; it is a biblical form. To borrow the rule we teach throughout this seminary: every sermon must be biblical, but not every sermon need be expository. A story drawn faithfully from the Word, carrying the truth of God into the heart of the hearer, is as biblical as any verse-by-verse exposition ever preached.

Basi tunarudi pale tulipoanzia. Yesu ndiye Msimulizi Mkuu wa hadithi, naye ndiye kielelezo ambacho kila mhubiri hupimwa kwacho. Ikiwa Mwana wa Mungu kwa kawaida alibeba kweli za ndani kabisa za mbinguni juu ya mgongo wa hadithi kuhusu mkulima, shilingi, au kijana mkaidi, basi mhubiri anayeidharau simulizi amejiweka juu ya Bwana wake. Kuhubiri kwa masimulizi si usaliti wa kuhubiri kwa Kibiblia; ni muundo wa Kibiblia. Tukiazima kanuni tunayoifundisha katika seminari hii yote: kila mahubiri lazima yawe ya Kibiblia, lakini si kila mahubiri yanahitaji kuwa ya kifafanuzi. Simulizi iliyochotwa kwa uaminifu kutoka katika Neno, ikibeba ukweli wa Mungu hadi moyoni mwa msikilizaji, ni ya Kibiblia kama ufafanuzi wowote wa mstari kwa mstari uliowahi kuhubiriwa.

Consider what this means. The God who could have handed us a systematic theology in numbered propositions instead gave us a library that is mostly story — a garden, a flood, a wandering family, a burning bush, a manger, an empty tomb. He did not do this because His people were too simple for doctrine; the same Bible contains Romans. He did it because He made us, and He knows that the human heart was built to be reached through the door of the story. When a preacher learns to tell a story well, he is not stooping to a lower form; he is taking up the very instrument his Maker chose. There is a humility in this, and a freedom. The humility is that our cleverest arguments are not the highest reach of the pulpit. The freedom is that the shyest preacher, who could never win a debate, can still sit a congregation on the edge of its seat with a tale well told — and carry the truth of God straight into the heart while he does it.

Tafakari maana ya jambo hili. Mungu ambaye angeweza kutupa theolojia ya kimfumo katika kauli zilizopangwa kwa namba badala yake alitupa maktaba ambayo kwa sehemu kubwa ni masimulizi — bustani, gharika, familia inayotangatanga, kichaka kinachowaka moto, hori la kulia ng'ombe, kaburi lililo tupu. Hakufanya hivyo kwa sababu watu wake walikuwa wajinga mno kwa mafundisho; Biblia hiyo hiyo ina kitabu cha Warumi. Alifanya hivyo kwa sababu Yeye ndiye aliyetuumba, naye anajua kwamba moyo wa mwanadamu uliumbwa kufikiwa kupitia mlango wa simulizi. Mhubiri anapojifunza kusimulia hadithi vizuri, hajishushi kwenye muundo duni; anachukua chombo kile kile ambacho Muumba wake alikichagua. Kuna unyenyekevu katika hili, na uhuru. Unyenyekevu ni kwamba hoja zetu za werevu zaidi si kilele cha juu kabisa cha mimbari. Uhuru ni kwamba mhubiri mwenye haya zaidi, ambaye hangeweza kamwe kushinda mdahalo, bado anaweza kulifanya kusanyiko liketi ukingoni mwa viti vyake kwa hadithi iliyosimuliwa vizuri — na kubeba ukweli wa Mungu moja kwa moja hadi moyoni huku akifanya hivyo.

A word of caution, which the later units will develop: the mandate is not a license. The story must always carry the truth of God, never entertain for its own sake; it must be honest and well-sourced, never embellished or stolen; it must serve the text, never replace it. Hold the freedom and the responsibility together, and you are ready to learn the craft. In the units ahead we will study how people learn, the three forms of the story sermon, how to preach the Bible's own narratives and its living characters, the parables of the Master, where to find and how to keep your illustrations, and finally how to tell a story so that it lands. How People Learn & the Right Brain
Jinsi Watu Wanavyojifunza & Ubongo wa Kulia

Stand before any congregation and you are speaking to more than one kind of mind. Some hearers follow a chain of reasoning like a staircase; others never come alive until you show them a picture. The preacher who knows only how to argue reaches only half the room. Before we take up the forms of the story sermon, we must understand how people actually receive truth — and why the imagination is not the enemy of the intellect but its partner.

Simama mbele ya kusanyiko lolote, nawe utakuwa unazungumza na zaidi ya aina moja ya akili. Baadhi ya wasikilizaji hufuata mfululizo wa hoja kama ngazi; wengine hawaamki kamwe hadi uwaonyeshe picha. Mhubiri anayejua tu kutoa hoja huwafikia nusu tu ya watu walio ukumbini. Kabla hatujashughulikia miundo ya mahubiri ya hadithi, lazima tuelewe jinsi watu wanavyopokea ukweli hasa — na kwa nini mawazo ya kubuni picha (taswira) si adui wa akili bali ni mshirika wake.
2.1 Three Ways People Learn
2.1 Njia Tatu za Watu Kujifunza
People do not all take in truth the same way. Following Solomon's observation, we may speak of at least three ways that people learn, and the wise preacher learns to use all three.
Watu wote hawapokei ukweli kwa njia ileile. Tukifuata maoni ya Solomon, tunaweza kusema kuna angalau njia tatu ambazo watu hujifunza, na mhubiri mwenye hekima hujifunza kuzitumia zote tatu.

First, the prose method. This is learning by logically developed, systematically and sequentially outlined summaries — lessons drawn in order from events, information, and data. It is the method most often used in preaching: the stated proposition, the numbered divisions, the orderly march from point to point. There is nothing wrong with it, and much of what this seminary teaches in its preaching course is devoted to doing it well. But it carries a hidden danger. Information may be conveyed without ever being received. The words leave the preacher's mouth, they even enter the hearer's ear, and yet they never lodge in the heart. This way of preaching would be perfectly sufficient if every person in the pew were Data, the android from Star Trek, able to absorb a stream of facts the way a computer downloads a file. But the people we preach to are not computers. They are tired, distracted, grieving, hoping human beings, and a list of true propositions slides off them like water off glass. The prose method is necessary; it is simply not, by itself, enough.

Kwanza, njia ya maelezo ya kawaida (nathari). Hii ni kujifunza kupitia mihtasari iliyokuzwa kwa mantiki, iliyopangwa kwa utaratibu na kwa mfuatano — mafundisho yanayotolewa kwa mpangilio kutoka katika matukio, taarifa, na takwimu. Ndiyo njia inayotumika mara nyingi zaidi katika kuhubiri: kauli kuu iliyotamkwa, migawanyo yenye namba, mwendo wa utaratibu kutoka hoja moja hadi nyingine. Hakuna kosa ndani yake, na sehemu kubwa ya yale ambayo seminari hii inafundisha katika kozi yake ya kuhubiri imejitoa katika kuifanya vizuri. Lakini ina hatari iliyofichika. Taarifa inaweza kupitishwa bila kupokelewa kamwe. Maneno yanatoka kinywani mwa mhubiri, yanaingia hata sikioni mwa msikilizaji, lakini hayatulii moyoni kamwe. Njia hii ya kuhubiri ingetosha kabisa kama kila mtu aliyeketi kitini angekuwa Data, roboti-binadamu (android) kutoka Star Trek, anayeweza kunyonya mkondo wa ukweli wa mambo jinsi kompyuta inavyopakua faili. Lakini watu tunaowahubiria si kompyuta. Ni wanadamu waliochoka, waliovurugika, wanaoomboleza, wanaotumaini, na orodha ya kauli za kweli huwateleza kama maji yanavyoteleza juu ya kioo. Njia ya nathari ni ya lazima; ila, peke yake, haitoshi.

Second, the visual method. This is learning by what the eye can see — drama, pictures, movement, the acted parable. Willow Creek Community Church built much of its ministry on the weekly use of drama, setting a scene before the congregation so the truth could be watched before it was explained. The eye is a door into the heart that the ear cannot always open. When the prophet Ezekiel lay on his side before a model of besieged Jerusalem, when Jeremiah smashed the potter's jar in the valley, when Jesus took a little child and set him in the midst, truth was being taught to the eye. The preacher who can paint a picture in words is using this same door.

Pili, njia ya kuona. Hii ni kujifunza kupitia kile ambacho jicho linaweza kuona — maigizo, picha, mwendo, mfano unaoigizwa. Kanisa la Willow Creek Community Church lilijenga sehemu kubwa ya huduma yake juu ya matumizi ya maigizo kila juma, likiweka tukio mbele ya kusanyiko ili ukweli uweze kutazamwa kabla haujaelezwa. Jicho ni mlango wa kuingia moyoni ambao sikio haliwezi kuufungua kila mara. Nabii Ezekieli alipolala kwa ubavu mbele ya kielelezo cha Yerusalemu uliozingirwa, Yeremia alipovunja gudulia la mfinyanzi bondeni, Yesu alipomchukua mtoto mdogo na kumweka katikati yao, ukweli ulikuwa ukifundishwa kwa jicho. Mhubiri anayeweza kuchora picha kwa maneno anatumia mlango huohuo.

Third, the story method. This is learning through symbols — using the image, the narrative, the concrete picture as the vehicle that carries ideas, concepts, facts, and information into the soul. We seem to absorb and assimilate truth far better through symbols than through the bare prose that only states the facts. This is not a third-rate substitute for argument, a concession to the simple. For most people, most of the time, the story is the most effective road into the heart — which is exactly why it was the road our Lord traveled most. The wise preacher will not choose one of these three methods and despise the others. He will learn to reach the logical hearer and the watching hearer and the story-shaped hearer in the very same message.

Tatu, njia ya hadithi. Hii ni kujifunza kupitia ishara — kutumia taswira, simulizi, picha halisi kama chombo kinachobeba mawazo, dhana, ukweli wa mambo, na taarifa hadi ndani ya nafsi. Inaonekana tunanyonya na kuuingiza ukweli ndani yetu vizuri zaidi kupitia ishara kuliko kupitia nathari tupu inayotaja tu ukweli wa mambo. Hii si mbadala wa daraja la tatu wa hoja, wala si msamaha kwa watu wa kawaida. Kwa watu wengi, mara nyingi, hadithi ndiyo njia yenye matokeo zaidi ya kuingia moyoni — na ndiyo sababu hasa ilikuwa njia ambayo Bwana wetu aliipita mara nyingi zaidi. Mhubiri mwenye hekima hatachagua njia moja kati ya hizi tatu na kuzidharau nyingine. Atajifunza kumfikia msikilizaji wa kimantiki, na msikilizaji anayetazama, na msikilizaji aliyeumbwa na hadithi, katika ujumbe uleule mmoja.

Notice that our Lord used all three. He reasoned — He silenced the Sadducees with a tight argument about the God of the living (Matthew 22:31–32). He taught the eye — He took bread and a cup and a basin of water and made the truth visible. And again and again He told stories. He did not rank the methods or apologize for the humblest; He used whichever one would carry the truth into a particular heart on a particular day. The preacher who masters only one method has narrowed the gate through which the gospel may reach his people. The preacher who learns all three has widened it.

Angalia kwamba Bwana wetu alizitumia zote tatu. Alitoa hoja — aliwanyamazisha Masadukayo kwa hoja thabiti kuhusu Mungu wa walio hai (Mathayo 22:31–32). Alifundisha jicho — alichukua mkate na kikombe na bakuli la maji akaufanya ukweli uonekane. Na tena na tena alisimulia hadithi. Hakuzipanga njia hizo kwa ubora wala hakuiombea radhi iliyo nyenyekevu kuliko zote; alitumia ile ambayo ingebeba ukweli hadi ndani ya moyo fulani siku fulani. Mhubiri anayemudu njia moja tu amepunguza upana wa lango ambalo kupitia hilo Injili inaweza kuwafikia watu wake. Mhubiri anayejifunza zote tatu amelipanua.
2.2 The Two Hemispheres
2.2 Pande Mbili za Ubongo
The teaching in this section is the contributed work of Andi Cook.
Mafundisho katika kifungu hiki ni kazi iliyochangiwa na Andi Cook.

In recent decades a way of describing the mind has become widely known: the theory of the "right" and the "left" brain. Generally speaking, each half of the brain tends to specialize in particular kinds of tasks. The left brain is the logical and analytical side — the brain of the scientist and the architect, the brain of the outline, the syllogism, the careful argument. The right brain is the creative side — the brain of the painter, the musician, and the poet, the brain of image, color, and metaphor. We need not press the science further than it will bear; as a way of picturing two real capacities in every person, it is illuminating and useful. Most of us lean to one side, and — here is the point for preachers — most preaching leans hard to the left. It defines, it divides, it proves. Meanwhile the people in front of us were made with both hemispheres, and the gospel is addressed to the whole person. A sermon that speaks only to the analytical half of a man and never knocks on the door of his imagination has left half of him untouched.

Katika miongo ya karibuni njia fulani ya kuieleza akili imejulikana sana: nadharia ya ubongo wa "kulia" na wa "kushoto." Kwa ujumla, kila nusu ya ubongo huelekea kubobea katika aina fulani za kazi. Ubongo wa kushoto ni upande wa mantiki na uchambuzi — ubongo wa mwanasayansi na wa msanifu majengo, ubongo wa muhtasari, wa hoja ya kimantiki (sillojismu), wa hoja iliyopangwa kwa uangalifu. Ubongo wa kulia ni upande wa ubunifu — ubongo wa mchoraji, wa mwanamuziki, na wa mshairi, ubongo wa taswira, rangi, na sitiari. Hatuhitaji kuisukuma sayansi hii mbali kuliko inavyoweza kustahimili; kama njia ya kuziwazia picha za uwezo halisi wa aina mbili ulio ndani ya kila mtu, inaangaza na ina manufaa. Wengi wetu huegemea upande mmoja, na — hapa ndipo hoja kwa wahubiri ilipo — mahubiri mengi huegemea sana upande wa kushoto. Yanafafanua, yanagawanya, yanathibitisha. Wakati huohuo watu walio mbele yetu waliumbwa na pande zote mbili za ubongo, na Injili inamwelekea mtu mzima. Mahubiri yanayozungumza tu na nusu ya mtu inayochambua, na kamwe hayabishi hodi kwenye mlango wa mawazo yake ya kubuni, yameiacha nusu yake bila kuiguswa.

Picture two people in the same pew. One is an engineer; he wants the argument to hold, the numbers to add up, the steps to follow in order, and if you give him that he is satisfied. Beside him sits an artist; the argument may be flawless and still leave her cold, but let one true image catch the light and her eyes fill, and she will carry that picture home and live by it for a year. Both came to hear from God. A sermon built only for the engineer leaves the artist starving in her seat; a sermon built only for the artist leaves the engineer unconvinced. The preacher is sent to feed them both at one table.

Wawazie watu wawili walioketi katika kiti kimoja kanisani. Mmoja ni mhandisi; anataka hoja isimame, hesabu zilingane, hatua zifuatane kwa mpangilio, na ukimpa hayo ameridhika. Kando yake ameketi msanii; hoja inaweza kuwa bila dosari na bado ikamwacha baridi, lakini acha taswira moja ya kweli ishike nuru, na macho yake yatajaa machozi, naye atabeba picha hiyo nyumbani na kuishi kwayo kwa mwaka mzima. Wote wawili walikuja kusikia kutoka kwa Mungu. Mahubiri yaliyojengwa kwa ajili ya mhandisi peke yake yanamwacha msanii akifa njaa kitini mwake; mahubiri yaliyojengwa kwa ajili ya msanii peke yake yanamwacha mhandisi bila kusadikishwa. Mhubiri ametumwa kuwalisha wote wawili katika meza moja.
2.3 Two Outlines from One Passage
2.3 Mihtasari Miwili Kutoka Kifungu Kimoja

From a single passage of Scripture we can build two very different outlines, and seeing them side by side makes the lesson concrete. Take Matthew 14:22–33 — Jesus walking on the water, and Peter sinking. A left-brain outline simply organizes the information. It lists what Jesus did (He made the disciples get into the boat, sent them to the other side, dismissed the crowd, went up the mountain to pray, and came to them on the water), then what the disciples did, then what Peter did, and so on — an orderly inventory of the facts of the text. Warren Wiersbe gives exactly such an outline of this passage. There is nothing false in it. But during the Middle Ages this kind of endlessly divided outline was the typical sermon, and you can still hear its descendants today, and the truth is that preaching is more than reciting the facts of a passage in order. It involves imagination, interpretation, and application.

Kutoka katika kifungu kimoja cha Maandiko tunaweza kujenga mihtasari miwili tofauti sana, na kuiona ikiwa kando kwa kando kunalifanya somo liwe halisi. Chukua Mathayo 14:22–33 — Yesu akitembea juu ya maji, na Petro akizama. Muhtasari wa ubongo wa kushoto hupanga tu taarifa. Unaorodhesha yale Yesu aliyofanya (aliwalazimisha wanafunzi waingie katika chombo, akawatanguliza ng'ambo, akauaga mkutano, akapanda mlimani kuomba, akawaendea juu ya maji), kisha yale wanafunzi waliyofanya, kisha yale Petro aliyofanya, na kadhalika — orodha ya utaratibu ya ukweli wa mambo katika kifungu. Warren Wiersbe anatoa muhtasari wa namna hiyo hasa wa kifungu hiki. Hakuna uongo ndani yake. Lakini katika Zama za Kati muhtasari wa aina hii, uliogawanywa bila mwisho, ndio uliokuwa mahubiri ya kawaida, na bado unaweza kuwasikia wazao wake leo, na ukweli ni kwamba kuhubiri ni zaidi ya kukariri ukweli wa mambo ya kifungu kwa mpangilio. Kunahusisha mawazo ya kubuni, tafsiri, na matumizi.

With very little effort the same passage yields a more "preachable" keyword outline. The subject might be the activities of Christ in our lives, and the divisions become: Jesus commands our lives — so obey Him; Jesus controls our circumstances — so trust Him; Jesus calms our fears — so worship Him (Wiersbe). That is a good outline, and far better than the bare inventory, because it has moved from information to application; it tells the hearer not only what happened on the lake but what to do on Monday. And yet — this is the door this unit wants to open — preaching can be more even than three well-turned, alliterated points.

Kwa juhudi kidogo sana kifungu hichohicho kinatoa muhtasari wa neno kiini ulio "rahisi kuhubiriwa" zaidi. Somo linaweza kuwa kazi za Kristo katika maisha yetu, na migawanyo inakuwa: Yesu anaamuru maisha yetu — kwa hiyo mtii; Yesu anatawala hali zetu — kwa hiyo mtumaini; Yesu anatuliza hofu zetu — kwa hiyo mwabudu (Wiersbe). Huo ni muhtasari mzuri, na bora zaidi kuliko orodha tupu, kwa sababu umesonga kutoka kwenye taarifa hadi kwenye matumizi; unamwambia msikilizaji si tu kilichotokea ziwani bali pia afanye nini Jumatatu. Na bado — huu ndio mlango ambao sehemu hii inataka kuufungua — kuhubiri kunaweza kuwa zaidi hata ya hoja tatu zilizoundwa vizuri zenye mwanzo unaofanana.

The difference between the two outlines is not that one is true and the other false; both are drawn from the same verses. The difference is what each one does to the hearer. The inventory informs him: he leaves knowing the order of events on the lake. The keyword outline instructs him: he leaves knowing what to do. But neither yet makes him feel the wind, or the lurch of the boat, or the cold grip of fear as the water closed over Peter's knees. That is the work reserved for the picture — and to the picture we now turn.

Tofauti kati ya mihtasari hii miwili si kwamba mmoja ni wa kweli na mwingine ni wa uongo; yote miwili imetolewa katika mistari ileile. Tofauti ni kile ambacho kila mmoja unamtendea msikilizaji. Orodha inampa taarifa: anaondoka akijua mpangilio wa matukio ziwani. Muhtasari wa neno kiini unamfundisha: anaondoka akijua afanye nini. Lakini hakuna hata mmoja kati ya hiyo unaomfanya bado auhisi upepo, au mtikisiko wa chombo, au mshiko baridi wa hofu maji yalipofunika magoti ya Petro. Hiyo ndiyo kazi iliyohifadhiwa kwa ajili ya picha — na sasa tunaigeukia picha.
2.4 The Controlling Metaphor
2.4 Sitiari Tawala

The highest reach of the right-brain sermon is the controlling metaphor. Here the imagination searches the passage not for more facts to list but for the one relationship, the one picture, that reveals the truth in a fresh and arresting way. For Matthew 14 the possibilities are many: "the storms of life," "Peter's boat experiences," "taking your eyes off Jesus," "a tested faith." Wiersbe's counsel is exact: "First, decide on the overriding metaphor (or symbol) that will control the development of the message." Notice the word control. Once the metaphor is chosen, it governs everything that follows — the introduction sets the picture, the movement develops it, the illustrations feed it, and the conclusion brings it home. The sermon is no longer a list held together by a number; it is a single image held together by its own inner life.

Kilele cha juu kabisa cha mahubiri ya ubongo wa kulia ni sitiari tawala. Hapa mawazo ya kubuni hukichunguza kifungu si ili kupata ukweli zaidi wa mambo wa kuorodhesha, bali ili kupata uhusiano mmoja, picha moja, inayofunua ukweli kwa njia mpya na ya kuvutia. Kwa Mathayo 14 uwezekano ni mwingi: "dhoruba za maisha," "uzoefu wa Petro katika chombo," "kuondoa macho yako kwa Yesu," "imani iliyojaribiwa." Shauri la Wiersbe ni sahihi kabisa: "Kwanza, amua sitiari kuu (au ishara) itakayotawala ukuzaji wa ujumbe." Angalia neno kutawala. Sitiari ikishachaguliwa, inaongoza kila kitu kinachofuata — utangulizi unaiweka picha, mwendo unaikuza, vielelezo vinailisha, na hitimisho linaifikisha nyumbani. Mahubiri si orodha tena iliyoshikamanishwa na namba; ni taswira moja iliyoshikamanishwa na uhai wake wa ndani.

The method is not limited to one text. Watch how a single metaphor cracks a passage open. Escaping temptation is like escaping a raging fire — and "God will provide a way of escape" (1 Corinthians 10:13). Decision-making is like standing at a fence and choosing a side (Deuteronomy 30, where Moses sets life and death before the people). Trusting God is like trusting a computer you do not fully understand but rely on every day (Exodus 3–4, where Moses argues with the God who has just told him what to do). Facing discouragement is like climbing a mountain so steep you cannot see the top (Romans 8:26ff, where the Spirit helps us in our weakness). In each case the metaphor accomplishes in an instant what a page of explanation could not: it lets the hearer see the truth. And sometimes the right-brain sermon will carry no conventional outline at all — the metaphor itself, or the story itself, runs from the first sentence to the last. We will take that up fully when we come to the three forms of the story sermon.

Njia hii haikomei kwenye kifungu kimoja. Tazama jinsi sitiari moja inavyokifungua kifungu. Kuepuka jaribu ni kama kuepuka moto mkali — na Mungu "atafanya na mlango wa kutokea" (1 Wakorintho 10:13). Kufanya maamuzi ni kama kusimama kwenye uzio na kuchagua upande (Kumbukumbu la Torati 30, ambapo Musa anaweka uzima na mauti mbele ya watu). Kumtumaini Mungu ni kama kuitumaini kompyuta usiyoielewa kikamilifu lakini unaitegemea kila siku (Kutoka 3–4, ambapo Musa anabishana na Mungu ambaye ametoka tu kumwambia afanye nini). Kukabiliana na kuvunjika moyo ni kama kupanda mlima mkali sana hata huwezi kuona kilele chake (Warumi 8:26 na kuendelea, ambapo Roho hutusaidia udhaifu wetu). Katika kila mfano, sitiari inatimiza kwa mara moja kile ambacho ukurasa mzima wa maelezo usingeweza: inamwezesha msikilizaji kuuona ukweli. Na wakati mwingine mahubiri ya ubongo wa kulia hayatakuwa na muhtasari wa kawaida hata kidogo — sitiari yenyewe, au hadithi yenyewe, inaenda kuanzia sentensi ya kwanza hadi ya mwisho. Tutalishughulikia hilo kikamilifu tutakapofikia miundo mitatu ya mahubiri ya hadithi.

One caution belongs here, and the later unit on the dangers of the story will press it harder. The controlling metaphor must rise out of the text, not be dropped on top of it. A clever picture that twists the passage to fit is worse than no picture at all, for it preaches the preacher's ingenuity instead of God's Word. Test every metaphor by asking whether it tells the truth about the text. "Taking your eyes off Jesus" genuinely belongs to Matthew 14, because that is precisely what sank Peter. Force a fashionable image onto a passage that will not bear it, and you have left the right brain and entered the wrong one.

Tahadhari moja inafaa hapa, na sehemu ya baadaye juu ya hatari za hadithi itaisisitiza zaidi. Sitiari tawala lazima itoke katika kifungu, isiangushwe juu yake. Picha ya werevu inayokipotosha kifungu ili kiifae ni mbaya kuliko kukosa picha kabisa, kwa maana inahubiri ujanja wa mhubiri badala ya Neno la Mungu. Ipime kila sitiari kwa kuuliza kama inasema kweli kuhusu kifungu. "Kuondoa macho yako kwa Yesu" ni mali ya Mathayo 14 kwa kweli, kwa sababu hicho ndicho hasa kilichomzamisha Petro. Lazimisha taswira inayopendwa na watu wa wakati huu juu ya kifungu kisichoweza kuibeba, nawe umeuacha ubongo wa kulia na kuingia katika ule usio sahihi.
2.5 Preaching to the Whole Person
2.5 Kumhubiria Mtu Mzima

Do not hear this unit as a call to abandon the logical sermon. The left brain is God's gift too. The careful division, the honest argument, the well-built outline are not the enemies of the gospel, and a preacher who throws them away in the name of imagination will soon be telling charming stories that mean nothing. The danger was never in using the analytical gifts; the danger is in stopping there — in addressing the reasoning half of a person and never reaching the half where his loves and his fears and his decisions actually live. Jesus reached both. In a single week He could reason with a lawyer over the greatest commandment and tell that same lawyer the story of a man going down to Jericho. The preacher's aim is the whole person: a sermon the mind can follow and the heart can feel, a sermon that is both true and unforgettable. In the next unit we turn from why the story works to how the story sermon is built — and we will meet its three classic forms.

Usiisikie sehemu hii kama wito wa kuyaacha mahubiri ya kimantiki. Ubongo wa kushoto nao ni zawadi ya Mungu. Mgawanyo wa uangalifu, hoja ya uaminifu, muhtasari uliojengwa vizuri si maadui wa Injili, na mhubiri anayevitupa kwa jina la mawazo ya kubuni hivi karibuni atakuwa akisimulia hadithi za kupendeza zisizo na maana yoyote. The Three Forms of the Story Sermon
Miundo Mitatu ya Mahubiri ya Hadithi

When a man sets out to preach a story sermon, the first question he usually asks is the wrong one. He asks, "Should I have an outline or not?" — as though that were the great divide. It is not. Outlined story sermons and outline-free story sermons have both been preached with power. The real question lies deeper: how will the story and the truth be joined? There are three classic answers — three forms the story sermon may take — and to learn them is to learn the architecture of narrative preaching.

Mtu anapoanza kuhubiri mahubiri ya hadithi, swali la kwanza analouliza kwa kawaida ndilo lisilo sahihi. Anauliza, "Je, niwe na muhtasari au la?" — kana kwamba hiyo ndiyo tofauti kubwa. Sivyo. Mahubiri ya hadithi yenye muhtasari na mahubiri ya hadithi yasiyo na muhtasari yote yamehubiriwa kwa nguvu. Swali halisi liko ndani zaidi: hadithi na ukweli vitaunganishwa vipi? Kuna majibu matatu ya kawaida — miundo mitatu ambayo mahubiri ya hadithi yanaweza kuchukua — na kuijifunza ni kujifunza usanifu wa kuhubiri kwa masimulizi.
3.1 Outline or No Outline?
3.1 Muhtasari au Bila Muhtasari?

Both have served the church well. The traditional sermon hangs its stories on a frame of numbered points; the pure story sermon may carry no visible frame at all — and yet it too is built, for every good story has a shape: a rising tension, a turn, a landing. Martin Thielen reminds us that "preaching is ultimately not about points on an outline but about helping people make contact with God." That is the liberating word, and every preacher chained to his three points needs to hear it: the outline was never the point. The encounter was always the point.

Yote mawili yamelitumikia kanisa vizuri. Mahubiri ya kimapokeo hutundika hadithi zake juu ya kiunzi cha hoja zenye namba; mahubiri ya hadithi tupu yanaweza kukosa kiunzi kinachoonekana kabisa — na bado nayo yamejengwa, kwa maana kila hadithi nzuri ina umbo: mvutano unaopanda, mgeuko, na kutua. Martin Thielen anatukumbusha kwamba "kuhubiri hatimaye hakuhusu hoja zilizo katika muhtasari bali kuwasaidia watu kukutana na Mungu." Hilo ndilo neno linaloweka huru, na kila mhubiri aliyefungwa kwa minyororo kwenye hoja zake tatu anahitaji kulisikia: muhtasari haukuwa kamwe ndio jambo kuu. Kukutana na Mungu ndiko kulikokuwa jambo kuu siku zote.

But hear Thielen rightly. He is not abolishing structure; he is dethroning it. A sermon with no structure at all is not a story sermon; it is a ramble, and a ramble has never helped anyone meet God. What we are about to learn are three structures — three disciplined ways of joining the story to the truth. Even the form that uses no points is a form. So lay down the false anxiety about outlines, and take up the better question in its place: of these three forms, which one does this text, this truth, and these people require? Solomon sets the three before us, and we will take them in turn.

Lakini msikie Thielen ipasavyo. Hafuti muundo; anauondoa kwenye kiti cha enzi. Mahubiri yasiyo na muundo wowote si mahubiri ya hadithi; ni porojo, na porojo hazijawahi kumsaidia mtu yeyote kukutana na Mungu. Tunachokaribia kujifunza ni miundo mitatu — njia tatu zenye nidhamu za kuiunganisha hadithi na ukweli. Hata ule muundo usiotumia hoja ni muundo. Kwa hiyo weka chini wasiwasi wa uongo juu ya mihtasari, na uchukue mahali pake swali lililo bora zaidi: kati ya miundo hii mitatu, ni upi ambao kifungu hiki, ukweli huu, na watu hawa wanauhitaji? Solomon anaiweka mitatu hii mbele yetu, nasi tutaichukua mmoja baada ya mwingine.
3.2 The Deductive Story Sermon — Point, Then Story
3.2 Mahubiri ya Hadithi ya Kideduktivu — Hoja, Kisha Hadithi

The first form is the one most of us were raised on. In the deductive story sermon the preacher states his points first, and then tells stories that serve as instances, case studies, or proofs of each point. The proposition is announced; the divisions are laid out; and under each division the story does its work of making the truth vivid and believable. This is the form the WiseSpeak method produces when its keyword outline is clothed with illustrations: Jesus calms our fears — so trust Him — and here is the story of the widow who learned to do exactly that.

Muundo wa kwanza ndio ambao wengi wetu tulilelewa nao. Katika mahubiri ya hadithi ya kideduktivu mhubiri hutaja hoja zake kwanza, kisha husimulia hadithi zinazotumika kama mifano, visa vya kuchunguzwa, au ushahidi wa kila hoja. Kauli kuu inatangazwa; migawanyo inapangwa; na chini ya kila mgawanyo hadithi hufanya kazi yake ya kuufanya ukweli uwe hai na wa kuaminika. Huu ndio muundo ambao mbinu ya WiseSpeak huuzaa muhtasari wake wa neno kiini unapovikwa vielelezo: Yesu anatuliza hofu zetu — kwa hiyo mtumaini — na hii hapa ni hadithi ya mjane aliyejifunza kufanya hivyo hasa.

The deductive form has real strengths. It is clear; the hearer always knows where he is and where he is going. It teaches well, because the truth is named plainly and then nailed down with a picture. And it is safe — the point can hardly be missed when it has already been spoken aloud. For instruction, for the patient building of doctrine, for the hearer who needs the truth handed to him in plain words, the deductive sermon is an honest and excellent servant. But it carries a quiet temptation, the very one Unit 1 warned against. Once the point has been announced, the story can shrink into mere filler — a decoration hung on a truth already delivered, a sweetener stirred into medicine that was already swallowed. The cure is to remember, even here, that the story is not the illustration of the message but the vehicle for it: the place where the truth actually enters the heart. Preach the deductive sermon freely, but let the story carry weight and not merely ornament.

Muundo wa kideduktivu una nguvu halisi. Ni wazi; msikilizaji daima anajua yuko wapi na anaelekea wapi. Unafundisha vizuri, kwa sababu ukweli unatajwa waziwazi kisha unakazwa kwa picha. Na ni salama — hoja haiwezi kukosekana kwa urahisi wakati imeshatamkwa kwa sauti. Kwa mafundisho, kwa ujenzi wa subira wa mafundisho ya imani, kwa msikilizaji anayehitaji kukabidhiwa ukweli kwa maneno ya wazi, mahubiri ya kideduktivu ni mtumishi mwaminifu na bora. Lakini yana kishawishi kimya, kilekile ambacho Sehemu ya 1 ilionya juu yake. Hoja ikishatangazwa, hadithi inaweza kusinyaa na kuwa kijaza-nafasi tu — pambo lililotundikwa juu ya ukweli uliokwisha kutolewa, sukari iliyokorogwa ndani ya dawa iliyokwisha kumezwa. Tiba ni kukumbuka, hata hapa, kwamba hadithi si kielelezo cha ujumbe bali ni chombo chake: mahali ambapo ukweli huingia moyoni hasa. Hubiri mahubiri ya kideduktivu kwa uhuru, lakini acha hadithi ibebe uzito na isiwe pambo tu.

Do not let the warnings make you despise this honest old form. A great deal of the best preaching in the history of the church has been deductive, and there are truths the people simply need stated, not smuggled. When a congregation is being battered by a false teaching, they do not need a subtle story that leaves them guessing; they need the truth named, defended, and illustrated until it stands like a wall. The deductive sermon builds that wall. Its plainness is not a weakness but a mercy to the hearer who has come, tired and confused, wanting only to be told plainly what God has said.

Usiache maonyo haya yakufanye uudharau muundo huu mwaminifu wa zamani. Sehemu kubwa ya mahubiri bora katika historia ya kanisa imekuwa ya kideduktivu, na kuna kweli ambazo watu wanahitaji tu kuambiwa waziwazi, si kuingizwa kwa kujificha. Kusanyiko linaposhambuliwa na fundisho la uongo, halihitaji hadithi ya hila inayowaacha wakibahatisha; linahitaji ukweli utajwe, utetewe, na uelezwe kwa vielelezo hadi usimame kama ukuta. Mahubiri ya kideduktivu hujenga ukuta huo. Uwazi wake si udhaifu bali ni rehema kwa msikilizaji aliyekuja, amechoka na kuchanganyikiwa, akitaka tu kuambiwa waziwazi kile Mungu alichosema.
3.3 The Inductive Story Sermon — Story, Then Point
3.3 Mahubiri ya Hadithi ya Kiinduktivu — Hadithi, Kisha Hoja

The second form reverses the order, and in reversing it discovers a strange power. In the inductive story sermon the preacher tells the story without giving away the point. He lets the congregation overhear it, be drawn into it, take sides in it — and only at the end, sometimes in a single sentence, does the point arrive, and the hearer discovers it as though he had thought of it himself. Why does this work so well? Because a point forced on a man at the front door raises his defenses, but a point he discovers for himself he owns. We resist being told; we cannot resist what we have seen with our own eyes.

Muundo wa pili unageuza mpangilio, na katika kuugeuza unagundua nguvu ya ajabu. Katika mahubiri ya hadithi ya kiinduktivu mhubiri husimulia hadithi bila kuifichua hoja. Analiacha kusanyiko liisikie kana kwamba kwa bahati, livutwe ndani yake, lichukue upande ndani yake — na mwishoni tu, wakati mwingine kwa sentensi moja, hoja hufika, na msikilizaji huigundua kana kwamba ameiwaza yeye mwenyewe. Kwa nini hii inafanya kazi vizuri hivi? Kwa sababu hoja inayolazimishwa juu ya mtu mlangoni pa mbele huinua ulinzi wake, lakini hoja anayoigundua mwenyewe anaimiliki. Tunakataa kuambiwa; hatuwezi kukataa kile tulichokiona kwa macho yetu wenyewe.

This is the method of Nathan, the purest example in all the Bible. He did not begin, "You, O king, are an adulterer and a murderer." He began, "There were two men in a certain city, the one rich and the other poor." David's anger blazed against the rich man of the story; the king passed judgment — and then the trap closed: "Thou art the man." The truth that would have been deflected as an accusation went home as a verdict the king had pronounced upon himself. Isaiah did the same with his vineyard song: the people enjoyed the music until they realized that they were the vineyard. This is why inductive preaching has sometimes been called letting people "overhear" the gospel — they listen freely because they do not yet know it is aimed at them.

Hii ndiyo njia ya Nathani, mfano ulio safi kuliko yote katika Biblia nzima. Hakuanza, "Wewe, Ee mfalme, ni mzinzi na mwuaji." Alianza, "Palikuwa na watu wawili katika mji mmoja; mmoja wao alikuwa tajiri, na wa pili maskini." Hasira ya Daudi iliwaka juu ya yule tajiri wa hadithi; mfalme akatoa hukumu — kisha mtego ukafunga: "Wewe ndiwe mtu huyo." Ukweli ambao ungekwepwa kama shtaka uliingia ndani kama hukumu ambayo mfalme alikuwa amejitamkia mwenyewe. Isaya alifanya vivyo hivyo kwa wimbo wake wa shamba la mizabibu: watu waliufurahia muziki hadi walipotambua kwamba wao ndio shamba la mizabibu. Ndiyo sababu kuhubiri kwa kiinduktivu wakati mwingine kumeitwa kuwaacha watu "waisikie kwa bahati" Injili — wanasikiliza kwa uhuru kwa sababu bado hawajui kwamba imeelekezwa kwao.

It was Fred Craddock who, more than anyone in the last century, recovered this method for the modern pulpit and gave it a name. In books with titles like As One Without Authority and Overhearing the Gospel, he argued that the preacher who hands down conclusions from on high will be tuned out by a generation that distrusts authority, while the preacher who walks the people through the same path of discovery he himself walked will carry them with him. The inductive sermon does not lecture from the mountaintop; it takes the congregation by the hand at the foot of the trail and climbs alongside them, so that they reach the summit together and the view is theirs because they earned the climb. This is not a trick of psychology; it is respect for the way God made the soul to learn.

Alikuwa Fred Craddock ambaye, zaidi ya mtu yeyote katika karne iliyopita, aliirejesha njia hii kwa mimbari ya kisasa na kuipa jina. Katika vitabu vyenye majina kama As One Without Authority (Kama Mtu Asiye na Mamlaka) na Overhearing the Gospel (Kuisikia Injili kwa Bahati), alihoji kwamba mhubiri anayeshusha mahitimisho kutoka juu atapuuzwa na kizazi kisichoamini mamlaka, ilhali mhubiri anayewaongoza watu katika njia ileile ya ugunduzi ambayo yeye mwenyewe aliipita atawabeba pamoja naye. Mahubiri ya kiinduktivu hayatoi hotuba kutoka kileleni mwa mlima; yanalishika kusanyiko mkono chini ya njia ya mlima na kupanda pamoja nalo, ili wafike kileleni pamoja na mandhari iwe yao kwa sababu walistahili kwa kupanda. Huu si ujanja wa saikolojia; ni heshima kwa jinsi Mungu alivyoiumba nafsi ijifunze.

The inductive form does not forbid points — a preacher may string together a series of inductive stories, each yielding its own discovery — but its genius is the withheld conclusion, the truth that dawns rather than the truth that is dumped. And its danger is the exact mirror of the deductive's. Where the deductive risks a point too baldly stated, the inductive risks a point too dimly landed. The discovery must actually be made; if the hearer goes home uncertain what he was meant to see, the sermon has failed for all its artistry. The skilled inductive preacher trusts his story to do the patient work — but he makes sure that, in the end, the lightning strikes.

Muundo wa kiinduktivu haukatazi hoja — mhubiri anaweza kuunganisha mfululizo wa hadithi za kiinduktivu, kila moja ikizaa ugunduzi wake — lakini ustadi wake ni hitimisho lililozuiliwa, ukweli unaopambazuka badala ya ukweli unaomwagwa. Na hatari yake ni kioo kamili cha ile ya kideduktivu. Pale ambapo mahubiri ya kideduktivu yanahatarisha hoja kutajwa kwa ukavu mno, ya kiinduktivu yanahatarisha hoja kutua kwa ufifi mno. Ugunduzi lazima ufanyike kweli; ikiwa msikilizaji anarudi nyumbani bila uhakika wa kile alichokusudiwa kuona, mahubiri yameshindwa licha ya ufundi wake wote. Mhubiri stadi wa kiinduktivu huiamini hadithi yake ifanye kazi ya subira — lakini anahakikisha kwamba, mwishowe, radi inapiga.
3.4 The Controlling-Story Sermon — One Story Throughout
3.4 Mahubiri ya Hadithi Tawala — Hadithi Moja Tangu Mwanzo Hadi Mwisho

The third form is the boldest. Here a single story dominates the entire sermon, running like a thread from the first sentence to the last. There may be other illustrations along the way, and there will certainly be discussion of the biblical text, but one story holds the whole message together, and the preacher keeps returning to it. Solomon offers a memorable example: a sermon built around a red Volkswagen that cheated its way out of a hospital parking lot. That one image — the little car at the gate, slipping away without paying — becomes the thread on which the entire sermon is strung. Whatever the preacher says, he keeps coming back to that picture, until it has done its full work in the hearer.

Muundo wa tatu ndio wenye ujasiri zaidi. Hapa hadithi moja inatawala mahubiri yote, ikipita kama uzi kuanzia sentensi ya kwanza hadi ya mwisho. Kunaweza kuwa na vielelezo vingine njiani, na hakika kutakuwa na majadiliano juu ya kifungu cha Biblia, lakini hadithi moja inaushikilia ujumbe wote pamoja, na mhubiri huendelea kuirudia. Solomon anatoa mfano unaokumbukwa: mahubiri yaliyojengwa kuzunguka gari jekundu aina ya Volkswagen lililotoroka kwa udanganyifu kutoka katika maegesho ya magari ya hospitali. Taswira hiyo moja — gari dogo langoni, likiteleza na kuondoka bila kulipa — inakuwa uzi ambao juu yake mahubiri yote yanatungwa. Lolote analosema mhubiri, huendelea kurudi kwenye picha hiyo, hadi imefanya kazi yake kamili ndani ya msikilizaji.

This is the narrative form in its fullest reach. Calvin Miller speaks of narratives as the longer, more involved stories — not the brief anecdote dropped beneath a point, but a sustained tale given room to breathe. Charles Bugg describes such preaching as a story, or a series of stories, with little interpretive material added — the story is trusted to carry the freight with a minimum of explanation laid on top. You will recognize this form at once as the natural extension of the controlling metaphor we met in Unit 2. There, a single image governed the message; here, a single story does. And it carries the same danger in a heightened degree. When one story rules a whole sermon, that story can quietly swallow the text, until the congregation goes home remembering the red Volkswagen and forgetting the Word of God it was meant to carry. The discipline, then, is to anchor the dominating story firmly to the Scripture it serves, so that the thread always leads back to the text and never away from it. A controlling story that has slipped its anchor is no longer preaching; it is a fine piece of theater.

Huu ndio muundo wa masimulizi katika upeo wake kamili. Calvin Miller anazungumza juu ya masimulizi kama hadithi ndefu zaidi, zenye kina zaidi — si kisa kifupi kinachodondoshwa chini ya hoja, bali hadithi inayoendelezwa na kupewa nafasi ya kupumua. Charles Bugg anaeleza kuhubiri kwa namna hiyo kuwa hadithi, au mfululizo wa hadithi, zikiwa na maelezo machache ya kufasiri yaliyoongezwa — hadithi inaaminiwa kubeba mzigo huku maelezo kidogo tu yakiwekwa juu yake. Utautambua muundo huu mara moja kuwa ni upanuzi wa kawaida wa sitiari tawala tuliyokutana nayo katika Sehemu ya 2. Huko, taswira moja iliongoza ujumbe; hapa, hadithi moja inaongoza. Na unabeba hatari ileile kwa kiwango cha juu zaidi. Hadithi moja inapotawala mahubiri yote, hadithi hiyo inaweza kukimeza kifungu kimyakimya, hadi kusanyiko linarudi nyumbani likikumbuka Volkswagen jekundu na kulisahau Neno la Mungu lililokusudiwa kubebwa nayo. Kwa hiyo nidhamu ni kuitia nanga hadithi hiyo inayotawala kwa uthabiti kwenye Maandiko inayoyatumikia, ili uzi daima urudi kwenye kifungu na kamwe usiende mbali nacho. Hadithi tawala iliyoachana na nanga yake si kuhubiri tena; ni mchezo mzuri wa kuigiza jukwaani.

Notice how much trust this form places in the preacher's judgment. A single illustration that fills a whole sermon had better be the right illustration, and it had better be true and well-earned — for if it is thin, the congregation will feel the thinness for thirty minutes instead of thirty seconds. The controlling story magnifies everything: a great story becomes unforgettable, and a weak or dishonest one becomes unbearable. This is why the later unit on the sources and ethics of illustration matters so much. The controlling-story sermon is the form that most rewards a preacher who has spent years quietly gathering good and truthful stories — and most punishes the one who has not.

Angalia jinsi muundo huu unavyoweka imani kubwa katika busara ya mhubiri. Kielelezo kimoja kinachojaza mahubiri yote ni afadhali kiwe kielelezo sahihi, na ni afadhali kiwe cha kweli na kilichostahiliwa — kwa maana kikiwa chembamba, kusanyiko litauhisi wembamba huo kwa dakika thelathini badala ya sekunde thelathini. Hadithi tawala hukuza kila kitu: hadithi kuu inakuwa isiyosahaulika, na hadithi dhaifu au isiyo ya uaminifu inakuwa isiyovumilika. Ndiyo sababu sehemu ya baadaye juu ya vyanzo na maadili ya vielelezo ina umuhimu mkubwa hivi. Mahubiri ya hadithi tawala ndiyo muundo unaomlipa zaidi mhubiri aliyetumia miaka mingi kukusanya kimyakimya hadithi nzuri na za kweli — na unamwadhibu zaidi yule ambaye hakufanya hivyo.
3.5 Choosing the Form
3.5 Kuchagua Muundo

How does the preacher decide among the three? The same way he decides everything in the pulpit: by asking what the text, the truth, the audience, and the occasion require. When the aim is clear instruction — a truth the people need stated plainly and fixed in memory — the deductive form serves them best. When the truth is one that would be resisted if it were announced outright, or one that strikes deeper when discovered than when declared, the inductive form is the wiser road; it was the road Nathan took to a guilty king. And when a single vivid truth can be carried by a single vivid story, the controlling-story form can do what neither of the others can — leave a whole congregation holding one unforgettable picture as they walk to their cars.

Mhubiri anaamuaje kati ya hiyo mitatu? Kwa njia ileile anayoamua kila kitu mimbarini: kwa kuuliza kile ambacho kifungu, ukweli, wasikilizaji, na tukio vinahitaji. Lengo likiwa mafundisho yaliyo wazi — ukweli ambao watu wanahitaji kuambiwa waziwazi na kuuweka katika kumbukumbu — muundo wa kideduktivu unawatumikia vizuri zaidi. Ukweli ukiwa ni ule ambao ungepingwa kama ungetangazwa moja kwa moja, au ule unaopenya ndani zaidi unapogunduliwa kuliko unapotangazwa, muundo wa kiinduktivu ndio njia yenye hekima zaidi; ilikuwa njia ambayo Nathani aliichukua kwa mfalme mwenye hatia. Na ukweli mmoja ulio hai ukiweza kubebwa na hadithi moja iliyo hai, muundo wa hadithi tawala unaweza kufanya kile ambacho hakuna kati ya ile mingine kinachoweza — kuliacha kusanyiko zima likiwa limeshika picha moja isiyosahaulika wanapotembea kuelekea magari yao.

Picture the decision in practice. You are to preach on the forgiveness of God from the parable of the prodigal son. If your people are doubting that God would ever receive them back, you might preach it inductively — simply retell the story of the boy and the running father, and let the doubting heart discover, in the father's embrace, that the door stands open. If your people understand grace well enough but live as though they must still earn it, you might preach it deductively — state the truth that God forgives freely, then prove it from the parable and three other passages until it is beyond dispute. The same text, the same Lord; a different door, chosen for the people in front of you.

Wazia uamuzi huo katika vitendo. Unatakiwa kuhubiri juu ya msamaha wa Mungu kutoka katika mfano wa mwana mpotevu. Ikiwa watu wako wana shaka kwamba Mungu angewahi kuwapokea tena, unaweza kuuhubiri kwa kiinduktivu — kusimulia tu hadithi ya kijana na baba anayekimbia, na kuuacha moyo wenye shaka ugundue, katika kumbatio la baba, kwamba mlango uko wazi. Ikiwa watu wako wanaielewa neema vizuri vya kutosha lakini wanaishi kana kwamba bado lazima waistahili kwa kazi, unaweza kuuhubiri kwa kideduktivu — kutaja ukweli kwamba Mungu husamehe bure, kisha kuuthibitisha kutoka katika mfano huo na vifungu vingine vitatu hadi usiwe na ubishi. Kifungu kilekile, Bwana yuleyule; mlango tofauti, uliochaguliwa kwa ajili ya watu walio mbele yako.

These are not rigid boxes. A wise sermon may open inductively, drawing the people in before they know where they are going, and then turn deductive once their guard is down, naming the truth and pressing it home. The forms are tools on a bench, not cells in a prison. What must never happen is for the form to become the master. The form is a servant — a servant of the message, and of the hearer's meeting with God. Choose it as you would choose a road: not for its own sake, but because it is the one that actually arrives. In the next unit we leave the question of form behind and walk into the richest quarry the storyteller owns — the Bible's own narratives — to learn how to preach the very stories that God Himself chose to tell.

Hii si masanduku magumu yasiyobadilika. Mahubiri yenye hekima yanaweza kuanza kwa kiinduktivu, yakiwavuta watu ndani kabla hawajajua wanakoelekea, kisha yakageuka kuwa ya kideduktivu mara ulinzi wao unaposhuka, yakiutaja ukweli na kuusisitiza. Miundo ni vyombo juu ya meza ya fundi, si vyumba katika gereza. Kisichopaswa kutokea kamwe ni muundo kuwa bwana. Muundo ni mtumishi — mtumishi wa ujumbe, na wa kukutana kwa msikilizaji na Mungu. Uchague kama ungechagua barabara: si kwa ajili yake yenyewe, bali kwa sababu ndiyo inayofika kweli. Katika sehemu inayofuata tunaliacha nyuma swali la muundo na kuingia katika machimbo tajiri kuliko yote anayoyamiliki msimulizi wa hadithi — masimulizi ya Biblia yenyewe — ili kujifunza jinsi ya kuhubiri hadithi zilezile ambazo Mungu Mwenyewe alichagua kuzisimulia.
