Preaching the Bible's Own Narratives
Kuhubiri Masimulizi ya Biblia Yenyewe

We have settled why the story works and learned the forms it may take. Now we walk into the richest quarry the preacher will ever own — the narratives of the Bible itself. More of Scripture is story than is anything else, and these are not stories men invented; they are the stories God chose to tell. But a biblical narrative is not preached merely by reading it aloud. It must be studied as a narrative and retold as a narrative, and there is a craft to both.

Tumeshathibitisha kwa nini simulizi hufanya kazi, na tumejifunza maumbo linaloweza kuchukua. Sasa tunaingia katika machimbo tajiri kuliko yote ambayo mhubiri atawahi kumiliki — masimulizi ya Biblia yenyewe. Sehemu kubwa ya Maandiko ni simulizi kuliko kitu kingine chochote, na hizi si hadithi walizobuni wanadamu; ni hadithi ambazo Mungu Mwenyewe alichagua kusimulia. Lakini simulizi la Biblia halihubiriwi kwa kulisoma kwa sauti tu. Lazima lichunguzwe kama simulizi na lisimuliwe upya kama simulizi, na kila moja ya hayo lina ufundi wake.
4.1 The Richest Quarry
4.1 Machimbo Tajiri Kuliko Yote

Open your Bible at random and you are far more likely to land in a story than in anything else. Genesis is story; the Exodus is story; Judges, Samuel, Kings, and Chronicles are story; the Gospels are story; Acts is story. Even the books we think of as doctrine are studded with narrative — Paul recounting his conversion, the writer of Hebrews parading the heroes of faith. God could have given us His revelation as a systematic outline; instead He gave us, in large part, a record of what He did and said among real people in real places. To preach these passages as narrative is therefore not a clever modern technique; it is simply preaching them the way they were given.

Fungua Biblia yako mahali popote bila kuchagua, na kuna uwezekano mkubwa zaidi utaangukia simulizi kuliko kitu kingine chochote. Mwanzo ni simulizi; Kutoka ni simulizi; Waamuzi, Samweli, Wafalme na Mambo ya Nyakati ni simulizi; Injili ni simulizi; Matendo ni simulizi. Hata vitabu tunavyovifikiria kuwa vya mafundisho vimejaa masimulizi — Paulo akisimulia kuongoka kwake, mwandishi wa Waebrania akiwapitisha mbele yetu mashujaa wa imani. Mungu angeweza kutupa ufunuo wake kama muhtasari wa kimfumo; badala yake, kwa sehemu kubwa, alitupa kumbukumbu ya yale aliyoyatenda na kuyasema kati ya watu halisi mahali halisi. Kwa hiyo kuhubiri vifungu hivi kama masimulizi si mbinu ya kisasa ya werevu; ni kuvihubiri tu jinsi vilivyotolewa.

There is a reason God taught us mostly by story rather than by syllogism. He wanted us to know Him not as a set of propositions but as a Person who acts — who walks in a garden, wrestles at a ford, weeps at a tomb. The narratives are not the husk around the doctrine; very often they are the way the doctrine was meant to be known, as the character of a God revealed in what He does.

Kuna sababu Mungu alitufundisha hasa kwa simulizi badala ya kwa hoja za kimantiki. Alitaka tumjue si kama mkusanyiko wa kauli za kweli bali kama Nafsi inayotenda — anayetembea bustanini, anayeshindana kivukoni, anayelia kaburini. Masimulizi si ganda linalofunika fundisho; mara nyingi sana ndiyo njia ambayo fundisho lilikusudiwa kujulikana, kama tabia ya Mungu inayofunuliwa katika yale anayoyatenda.

And yet many a preacher takes one of God's living stories and grinds it into three lifeless abstractions, draining away the very blood that made it a story in the first place. The Bible says David ran toward Goliath; the abstract sermon says, "Point one: courage." The Bible shows the prodigal's father lifting his robes and running down the road; the abstract sermon says, "Point two: God's love." The truth in those points is real, but the form has thrown away the power. To preach a narrative as a narrative is to let David run and the father run before our eyes — and only then to say what their running means. But you cannot retell vividly what you have not first seen clearly. So before we retell, we must learn to study.

Hata hivyo, wahubiri wengi huchukua mojawapo ya hadithi hai za Mungu na kuisaga ikawa mawazo matatu ya kinadharia yasiyo na uhai, wakiikamua damu ileile iliyoifanya kuwa simulizi tangu mwanzo. Biblia inasema Daudi alikimbia kumwelekea Goliathi; mahubiri ya kinadharia yanasema, "Hoja ya kwanza: ujasiri." Biblia inamwonyesha baba wa mwana mpotevu akipandisha mavazi yake na kukimbia barabarani; mahubiri ya kinadharia yanasema, "Hoja ya pili: upendo wa Mungu." Kweli iliyo katika hoja hizo ni halisi, lakini umbo limetupilia mbali nguvu. Kuhubiri simulizi kama simulizi ni kumwacha Daudi akimbie na baba akimbie mbele ya macho yetu — na hapo tu ndipo tuseme kukimbia kwao kunamaanisha nini. Lakini huwezi kusimulia upya kwa uwazi kitu ambacho hujakiona kwanza kwa uwazi. Kwa hiyo kabla ya kusimulia upya, lazima tujifunze kuchunguza.
4.2 Three Steps Before You Preach
4.2 Hatua Tatu Kabla ya Kuhubiri

Solomon gives three simple steps for using the Bible in storytelling, and they form the frame of all that follows. First, understand the audience. You are not retelling the story into the air; you are bringing it to particular people with particular wounds, doubts, and hopes, and what they need from the story will shape how you tell it. Second, understand the text. This is the patient labor of study, and we will give the rest of this unit to it, because a hazy grasp of the passage produces a hazy sermon. Third, translate the text into the modern context. The story happened long ago and far away, and the bridge from that world to this one must be built on purpose, so that the hearer does not merely learn about an ancient event but feels it as the first audience felt it. Audience, text, translation — know your people, know your passage, and carry the one to the other.

Solomon anatoa hatua tatu rahisi za kutumia Biblia katika usimulizi wa hadithi, nazo zinaunda kiunzi cha yote yanayofuata. Kwanza, waelewe wasikilizaji. Husimulii hadithi hewani; unaileta kwa watu fulani wenye majeraha, mashaka na matumaini yao, na kile wanachohitaji kutoka kwenye hadithi kitaunda jinsi utakavyoisimulia. Pili, lielewe andiko. Hii ni kazi ya subira ya kujifunza, nasi tutatoa sehemu iliyobaki ya somo hili kwa ajili yake, kwa sababu ufahamu hafifu wa kifungu huzaa mahubiri hafifu. Tatu, litafsiri andiko katika mazingira ya kisasa. Hadithi ilitokea zamani sana na mbali sana, na daraja kutoka ulimwengu ule hadi huu lazima lijengwe kwa makusudi, ili msikilizaji asijifunze tu kuhusu tukio la kale bali alihisi kama wasikilizaji wa kwanza walivyolihisi. Wasikilizaji, andiko, tafsiri — wajue watu wako, kijue kifungu chako, na ubebe kimoja kukipeleka kwa kingine.
4.3 Studying the Narrative
4.3 Kuchunguza Simulizi

How do you "understand the text" of a story? Warren Wiersbe offers a study guide that turns a flat passage into a living scene, and it works by looking through five windows. Look first at the text itself — where this story stands in the whole message of the book, and where it stands in its immediate section, because a story cut from its setting will be misread. Look next at the people — their history before this moment, their relationship to one another, what became of them afterward and why, and whether Scripture mentions them anywhere else. Look at the places — why this location matters in the narrative, what the names mean (and what any name-changes mean), and what we know of the site from history and archaeology. Look at the events — list them in order, fix them in their time, ask what motives drove the people, what consequences followed, and how the same scene looked through the eyes of each person standing in it. And look, finally, at the speakers — who speaks, to whom, why, and how; what their words reveal about them; what follows from each speech; and, just as importantly, where there are silences, what is left unsaid, and which words and phrases are repeated.

Unawezaje "kuelewa andiko" la simulizi? Warren Wiersbe anatoa mwongozo wa kujifunza unaogeuza kifungu kisicho na uhai kuwa tukio hai, nao hufanya kazi kwa kuangalia kupitia madirisha matano. Angalia kwanza andiko lenyewe — hadithi hii imesimama wapi katika ujumbe mzima wa kitabu, na imesimama wapi katika sehemu yake ya karibu, kwa sababu hadithi iliyokatwa kutoka mazingira yake itaeleweka vibaya. Angalia kisha watu — historia yao kabla ya wakati huu, uhusiano wao wao kwa wao, kilichowapata baadaye na kwa nini, na kama Maandiko yanawataja mahali pengine popote. Angalia mahali — kwa nini eneo hili lina umuhimu katika simulizi, majina yanamaanisha nini (na mabadiliko yoyote ya majina yanamaanisha nini), na tunajua nini kuhusu eneo hilo kutokana na historia na akiolojia. Angalia matukio — yaorodheshe kwa mpangilio, yaweke katika wakati wake, uliza ni nia gani zilizowasukuma watu, ni matokeo gani yaliyofuata, na tukio lilelile lilionekanaje kupitia macho ya kila mtu aliyesimama ndani yake. Na mwisho, angalia wazungumzaji — nani anazungumza, kwa nani, kwa nini, na jinsi gani; maneno yao yanafunua nini kuwahusu; nini kinafuata kila usemi; na, jambo lenye umuhimu uleule, mahali palipo na ukimya, kile kisichosemwa, na maneno na misemo ipi inarudiwa.

Do not hear this as a checklist to be endured. Hear it as five doors, and behind every door is a sermon. The "future history" of a person — what became of him — is a sermon. A repeated phrase is a sermon. A telling silence is a sermon. The preacher who learns to study a narrative through these five windows will never again stand on a Saturday night with nothing to say; his problem will be the happy one of having found more than he can preach in a single sitting. Study is not the enemy of the vivid sermon. Study is its fuel. The richest retellings come from the preachers who have seen the scene most clearly.

Usiusikie huu kama orodha ya kuvumiliwa. Usikie kama milango mitano, na nyuma ya kila mlango kuna mahubiri. "Historia ya baadaye" ya mtu — kilichompata — ni mahubiri. Msemo unaorudiwa ni mahubiri. Ukimya wenye maana ni mahubiri. Mhubiri anayejifunza kuchunguza simulizi kupitia madirisha haya matano hatasimama tena Jumamosi usiku bila la kusema; tatizo lake litakuwa lile la furaha la kupata zaidi ya anavyoweza kuhubiri kwa kikao kimoja. Kujifunza si adui wa mahubiri yenye uhai. Kujifunza ndiko kuni zake. Masimulizi-upya tajiri kuliko yote hutoka kwa wahubiri ambao wameliona tukio kwa uwazi kuliko wote.

Let one window show its power. Take the "future history" of a person — what became of him after the scene closes. The rich young ruler walks away sorrowful, and the text lets him go; but study his future and you may preach the tragedy of the almost-saved, the man who stood near the kingdom and chose his portfolio instead. Or take a repeated word. In the parable of the prodigal the father says twice that his son "was dead, and is alive again; was lost, and is found" — and that repetition, studied, becomes the spine of a sermon on the homecoming grace works in a single afternoon. One window, patiently opened, and the sermon is already there.

Acha dirisha moja lionyeshe nguvu yake. Chukua "historia ya baadaye" ya mtu — kilichompata baada ya tukio kufungwa. Kijana mtawala tajiri anaondoka kwa huzuni, na andiko linamwacha aende; lakini ichunguze historia yake ya baadaye na unaweza kuhubiri msiba wa aliyekaribia kuokoka, mtu aliyesimama karibu na ufalme akachagua mali zake badala yake. Au chukua neno linalorudiwa. Katika mfano wa mwana mpotevu, baba anasema mara mbili kwamba mwanawe "alikuwa amekufa, naye amefufuka; alikuwa amepotea, naye ameonekana" — na marudio hayo, yakichunguzwa, yanakuwa uti wa mgongo wa mahubiri juu ya kurudi nyumbani ambako neema hutenda katika alasiri moja tu. Dirisha moja, likifunguliwa kwa subira, na mahubiri tayari yapo.
4.4 Retelling Without Adding
4.4 Kusimulia Upya Bila Kuongeza

Now we come to the heart of the matter, and to a line that must never be crossed. When you retell a Bible story, you may — and should — tell it vividly, "with embellishment," as the old preachers said. You may give the storm its howl and its spray; you may let the congregation feel the lurch of Peter's stomach as the water took his weight; you may render the heat of the noon sun on the road to Emmaus and the ache in two grieving hearts. This is sanctified imagination, and it is not only permitted but commanded by the very nature of the task, for a scene the preacher will not make live is a scene the hearer will not enter.

Sasa tunafika kwenye kiini cha jambo, na kwenye mstari ambao kamwe haupaswi kuvukwa. Unaposimulia upya hadithi ya Biblia, unaweza — na unapaswa — kuisimulia kwa uwazi wenye uhai, "kwa kuipamba," kama wahubiri wa zamani walivyosema. Unaweza kuipa dhoruba mlio wake na manyunyu yake; unaweza kuliacha kusanyiko lihisi tumbo la Petro likishtuka maji yalipobeba uzito wake; unaweza kuonyesha joto la jua la adhuhuri kwenye njia ya Emau na uchungu wa mioyo miwili yenye huzuni. Huu ni ubunifu uliotakaswa (sanctified imagination), na si tu unaruhusiwa bali unaamriwa na asili yenyewe ya kazi hii, kwa maana tukio ambalo mhubiri hatalifanya liwe hai ni tukio ambalo msikilizaji hataliingia.

But here is the line: sanctified imagination may color what Scripture has drawn; it may never contradict the text, invent events that change its meaning, or put new words into the mouth of God. You may imagine the look on the prodigal's face; you may not invent a second son who was never there. You may render Peter's fear; you may not have Jesus say something He never said. The Bible itself sets this boundary in iron: "Ye shall not add unto the word which I command you" (Deuteronomy 4:2); "Add thou not unto his words, lest he reprove thee" (Proverbs 30:6); and the solemn warning at the very end of the canon (Revelation 22:18). The freedom is wide — make the scene breathe — but the limit is absolute: it must remain the scene God actually gave. The discipline that keeps the two in balance is simple to state and hard to practice: test every added detail against the text, and keep only what the text could bear. Color inside the lines God has drawn, and the picture is still His; color outside them, and it has become yours.

Lakini huu ndio mstari: ubunifu uliotakaswa unaweza kutia rangi kile ambacho Maandiko yamechora; kamwe hauwezi kulipinga andiko, kubuni matukio yanayobadilisha maana yake, au kutia maneno mapya kinywani mwa Mungu. Unaweza kuwazia sura ya uso wa mwana mpotevu; huwezi kubuni mwana wa pili ambaye hakuwahi kuwepo. Unaweza kuonyesha hofu ya Petro; huwezi kumfanya Yesu aseme kitu ambacho hakuwahi kusema. Biblia yenyewe inaweka mpaka huu kwa chuma: "Msiliongeze neno niwaamurulo" (Kumbukumbu la Torati 4:2); "Usiongeze neno katika maneno yake; asije akakulaumu" (Mithali 30:6); na onyo zito mwishoni kabisa mwa orodha ya vitabu vitakatifu (Ufunuo 22:18). Uhuru ni mpana — lifanye tukio lipumue — lakini kikomo ni kamili: lazima libaki tukio lile ambalo Mungu alilitoa kweli. Nidhamu inayoshikilia mambo haya mawili katika uwiano ni rahisi kuitaja na ngumu kuitekeleza: pima kila undani ulioongezwa kwa kulinganisha na andiko, na ubakize tu kile ambacho andiko lingeweza kukibeba. Paka rangi ndani ya mistari ambayo Mungu ameichora, na picha bado ni yake; paka rangi nje yake, na imekuwa yako.

One vivid way to retell a narrative is to step inside it and preach in the first person — to stand in the pulpit as Peter, or as the woman at the well, and let the congregation hear the story from the lips of one who lived it. Done well, this collapses the distance of centuries; the hearer is no longer studying an ancient man but listening to him. Yet the same iron rule governs it: you may give the character the feelings and the senses the text implies, but you may not put into his mouth a confession the text denies him, or make him say what Scripture never let him say. The costume is imagination's; the script must remain the Bible's.

Njia moja yenye uhai ya kusimulia upya simulizi ni kuingia ndani yake na kuhubiri kwa nafsi ya kwanza — kusimama mimbarini kama Petro, au kama yule mwanamke kisimani, na kuliacha kusanyiko liisikie hadithi kutoka midomoni mwa mmoja aliyeiishi. Ikifanywa vizuri, hii inafuta umbali wa karne nyingi; msikilizaji hamchunguzi tena mtu wa kale bali anamsikiliza. Lakini kanuni ileile ya chuma inaitawala: unaweza kumpa mhusika hisia na milango ya fahamu ambayo andiko linadokeza, lakini huwezi kutia kinywani mwake ungamo ambalo andiko linamnyima, au kumfanya aseme kile ambacho Maandiko hayakumwacha aseme. Mavazi ni ya ubunifu; hati ya maneno (script) lazima ibaki kuwa ya Biblia.
4.5 Contemporizing the Story — A Worked Example
4.5 Kusasisha Hadithi — Mfano Uliofanyiwa Kazi

The last step is to bring the ancient scene near, to "contemporize" it so the hearer feels it in his own world. Sometimes a single modern phrase does it: the spies returning from Canaan with their report — "I've got some good news and some bad news"; Peter stepping out of the boat and discovering there is nothing underfoot — "Lord, where are the stumps?" A touch of humor can serve here, provided it brings the scene near rather than mocking the sacred. Contemporizing is the moment the bridge of step three actually carries weight, when a story two thousand years old happens, suddenly, to people sitting in folding chairs on a Sunday morning.

Hatua ya mwisho ni kulileta tukio la kale karibu, "kulisasisha" (contemporize) ili msikilizaji alihisi katika ulimwengu wake mwenyewe. Wakati mwingine msemo mmoja wa kisasa unatosha: wapelelezi wakirudi kutoka Kanaani na taarifa yao — "Nina habari njema na habari mbaya"; Petro akishuka kutoka mashuani na kugundua hakuna kitu chini ya miguu yake — "Bwana, visiki viko wapi?" Mguso wa ucheshi unaweza kusaidia hapa, mradi unalileta tukio karibu badala ya kudhihaki kilicho kitakatifu. Kusasisha ni wakati ambapo daraja la hatua ya tatu linabeba uzito kweli, pale hadithi ya miaka elfu mbili inapowatokea, ghafla, watu walioketi kwenye viti vya kukunja Jumapili asubuhi.

Consider a worked example — Dr. Cook's sermon on Matthew 16:13–18, "Whom do men say that I am." Jesus asks the disciples who the crowds think He is, and they run down the popular list, and the preacher does not hurry past the list but brings each name to life. Some said John the Baptist — and here is John, the strange cousin in the wilderness, his diet of locusts and honey, his clothing of animal skins, his thundering call to repentance, until the dance of a girl and the spite of a queen cost him his head on a platter. Some said Elijah — the prophet of fire, who shut the heavens for three and a half years and called down flame on a water-soaked altar while the prophets of Baal screamed at a silent sky. Some said Jeremiah — the weeping prophet, ridiculed and beaten, who preached judgment to a people who would not hear and was counted a failure in his own day. Each portrait makes the reader feel why people reached for that comparison when they looked at Jesus.

Fikiria mfano uliofanyiwa kazi — mahubiri ya Dkt. Cook juu ya Mathayo 16:13–18, "Watu hunena Mwana wa Adamu kuwa ni nani?" Yesu anawauliza wanafunzi umati unafikiri Yeye ni nani, nao wanaipitia orodha ya maoni ya watu, na mhubiri haipiti orodha hiyo kwa haraka bali analifanya kila jina kuwa hai. Wengine walisema Yohana Mbatizaji — na huyu hapa Yohana, binamu wa ajabu jangwani, chakula chake cha nzige na asali, mavazi yake ya ngozi za wanyama, mwito wake wa toba wenye ngurumo, hadi ngoma ya msichana mmoja na chuki ya malkia vilipomgharimu kichwa chake juu ya sinia. Wengine walisema Eliya — nabii wa moto, aliyezifunga mbingu kwa miaka mitatu na nusu na kuita moto ushuke juu ya madhabahu iliyolowa maji huku manabii wa Baali wakipiga kelele kwa anga lililonyamaza. Wengine walisema Yeremia — nabii wa machozi, aliyedhihakiwa na kupigwa, aliyehubiri hukumu kwa watu ambao hawangesikia, na akahesabiwa kuwa ameshindwa katika siku zake. Kila picha inamfanya msomaji ahisi kwa nini watu walichukua ulinganisho huo walipomtazama Yesu.

Then comes the contemporizing turn. Having retold the ancient guesses, the sermon carries the same question to the modern street corner: the Muslim says Jesus was a prophet, but less than Muhammad; the Jew says a great man, a founder of a religion; the secularist says the greatest teacher of all time, an example to follow. A popular play of recent decades asks Christ over and over, "Who are you?" — and never gives an answer, because the secular mind, left to itself, never can. And only when every ancient and modern voice has failed does Peter's confession land with its full weight: "Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God." That is the architecture of a narrative sermon: the scene retold until it lives, the question carried across the bridge into the present, and the truth of the text — here, the identity of Christ — left standing alone when every substitute has fallen away. Study the passage until you see it; retell it until they see it; contemporize it until it finds them; and never, in all your coloring, add a single stroke the Author did not draw. In the next unit we narrow our focus from the whole narrative to a single figure within it, and take up the ancient and powerful craft of biographical preaching.

Kisha kunakuja mgeuko wa kusasisha. Baada ya kusimulia upya makisio ya kale, mahubiri yanalibeba swali lilelile hadi kwenye pembe ya mtaa wa kisasa: Mwislamu anasema Yesu alikuwa nabii, lakini mdogo kuliko Muhammad; Myahudi anasema alikuwa mtu mkuu, mwanzilishi wa dini; mtu wa kidunia asiyejali dini anasema alikuwa mwalimu mkuu kuliko wote wa nyakati zote, kielelezo cha kufuata. Mchezo mmoja maarufu wa kuigiza wa miongo ya karibuni unamuuliza Kristo tena na tena, "Wewe ni nani?" — na kamwe hautoi jibu, kwa sababu akili ya kidunia, ikiachwa peke yake, haiwezi kamwe. Na ni pale tu kila sauti ya kale na ya kisasa imeshindwa ndipo ungamo la Petro linatua kwa uzito wake wote: "Wewe ndiwe Kristo, Mwana wa Mungu aliye hai." Huo ndio usanifu wa mahubiri ya masimulizi: tukio linasimuliwa upya hadi liwe hai, swali linabebwa kuvuka daraja hadi wakati wa sasa, na kweli ya andiko — hapa, utambulisho wa Kristo — inaachwa imesimama peke yake wakati kila kibadala kimeanguka. Kichunguze kifungu hadi ukione; kisimulie upya hadi wao wakione; kisasishe hadi kiwafikie; na kamwe, katika upakaji rangi wako wote, usiongeze hata mstari mmoja ambao Mwandishi hakuuchora. Biographical Preaching
Kuhubiri kwa Wasifu

From the whole narrative we now narrow the lens to a single life. Biographical preaching takes one person of Scripture — a David, a Jezebel, a Peter, a thief on a cross — and preaches the truth of God through the story of that person. It is one of the oldest and most powerful forms in the pulpit, and the Bible is full of it. But like every form, it has its own craft to master and its own danger to avoid.

Kutoka kwa simulizi zima sasa tunapunguza mtazamo hadi kwenye maisha ya mtu mmoja. Kuhubiri kwa wasifu huchukua mtu mmoja wa Maandiko — Daudi, Yezebeli, Petro, mnyang'anyi msalabani — na kuihubiri kweli ya Mungu kupitia hadithi ya mtu huyo. Ni mojawapo ya maumbo ya kale na yenye nguvu zaidi mimbarini, na Biblia imejaa umbo hili. Lakini kama kila umbo, lina ufundi wake wa kuumudu na hatari yake ya kuiepuka.
5.1 What Biographical Preaching Is
5.1 Kuhubiri kwa Wasifu ni Nini

Andrew Blackwood, who taught a generation to do this well, describes biographical preaching simply: it is the preaching of a Bible truth through the life of a Bible person. The subject is not really the man; the subject is the truth of God that his life displays. We do not preach Abraham in order to admire Abraham; we preach the faith of God's friend so that our hearers will trust the same God. The life is the window, and the light that comes through it is the truth.

Andrew Blackwood, aliyefundisha kizazi kizima kufanya hivi vizuri, anaeleza kuhubiri kwa wasifu kwa urahisi: ni kuhubiri kweli ya Biblia kupitia maisha ya mtu wa Biblia. Kwa kweli somo si mtu mwenyewe; somo ni kweli ya Mungu ambayo maisha yake yanaionyesha. Hatumhubiri Ibrahimu ili tumstaajabie Ibrahimu; tunaihubiri imani ya rafiki wa Mungu ili wasikilizaji wetu wamtumaini Mungu yuleyule. Maisha ni dirisha, na nuru inayopita ndani yake ni kweli.

This is not a method the church invented; it is a method the Bible models. Hebrews 11 is one long biographical sermon — Abel, Enoch, Noah, Abraham, Moses, Rahab, and a crowd of others, each life held up to preach the single truth that the just shall live by faith. And Paul tells us plainly why these lives were written down: "Now all these things happened unto them for examples: and they are written for our admonition" (1 Corinthians 10:11). The stories of Scripture's people were recorded on purpose, as examples and as warnings, for the instruction of everyone who would come after. When you preach a Bible character, you are not borrowing a technique from literature; you are doing what the Holy Spirit Himself did when He filled the Bible with lives. At this seminary the Bible Characters courses are this very discipline at work — the careful study and proclamation of Scripture's people, one life at a time.

Hii si mbinu ambayo kanisa liliibuni; ni mbinu ambayo Biblia inaionyesha kwa mfano. Waebrania 11 ni mahubiri marefu ya wasifu — Habili, Henoko, Nuhu, Ibrahimu, Musa, Rahabu, na umati wa wengine, kila maisha yakiinuliwa kuhubiri kweli moja kwamba mwenye haki ataishi kwa imani. Na Paulo anatuambia waziwazi kwa nini maisha haya yaliandikwa: "Basi mambo hayo yaliwapata wao kwa jinsi ya mfano; nayo yaliandikwa ili kutuonya sisi" (1 Wakorintho 10:11). Hadithi za watu wa Maandiko ziliandikwa kwa makusudi, kama mifano na kama maonyo, kwa mafundisho ya kila mtu atakayekuja baadaye. Unapomhubiri mhusika wa Biblia, huazimi mbinu kutoka kwa fasihi; unafanya kile ambacho Roho Mtakatifu Mwenyewe alifanya alipoijaza Biblia kwa maisha ya watu. Katika seminari hii, kozi za Wahusika wa Biblia ni nidhamu hii hasa ikitendwa — kujifunza kwa makini na kuwatangaza watu wa Maandiko, maisha moja baada ya jingine.
5.2 Why Preach Biography
5.2 Kwa Nini Kuhubiri Wasifu

Why does this form work so well? First, because people are interested in people. We may yawn at an abstract argument, but lean forward at a human story, and a truth embodied in a life becomes concrete, personal, and unforgettable where the same truth stated baldly slides away. Tell a man that pride goes before a fall and he nods; walk him through the rise and ruin of a proud king and he never forgets it. Second, because biography gives the hearer both kinds of help he needs: examples to follow and warnings to heed. Some lives are patterns — the faith of Abraham, the courage of Daniel, the loyalty of Ruth — and some are cautions — the compromise of Lot, the rebellion of Saul, the greed of Gehazi. The pulpit needs both, and biography supplies both. Third, because a single life can show the dealings of God stretched over time. A doctrine states that God is faithful; a life like Joseph's lets the congregation watch that faithfulness work through twenty years of pit, prison, and palace until it stands vindicated. There is a reason the deepest revelation God ever gave was not a list of attributes but a Person; truth lodges in us most deeply when we see it lived.

Kwa nini umbo hili hufanya kazi vizuri hivi? Kwanza, kwa sababu watu huvutiwa na watu. Huenda tukapiga miayo mbele ya hoja ya kinadharia, lakini tunainama mbele kusikiliza hadithi ya binadamu, na kweli iliyovikwa katika maisha inakuwa halisi, ya kibinafsi, na isiyosahaulika, pale ambapo kweli ileile ikitamkwa kavu huteleza na kupotea. Mwambie mtu kwamba kiburi hutangulia anguko naye atatikisa kichwa; mpitishe katika kuinuka na kuangamia kwa mfalme mwenye kiburi naye hatasahau kamwe. Pili, kwa sababu wasifu humpa msikilizaji aina zote mbili za msaada anazohitaji: mifano ya kufuata na maonyo ya kuzingatia. Maisha mengine ni vielelezo — imani ya Ibrahimu, ujasiri wa Danieli, uaminifu wa Ruthu — na mengine ni tahadhari — ulegevu wa Lutu, uasi wa Sauli, tamaa ya Gehazi. Mimbari inahitaji yote mawili, na wasifu hutoa yote mawili. Tatu, kwa sababu maisha ya mtu mmoja yanaweza kuonyesha matendo ya Mungu yaliyonyoshwa kwa muda mrefu. Fundisho linasema kwamba Mungu ni mwaminifu; maisha kama ya Yusufu yanaliwezesha kusanyiko kuutazama uaminifu huo ukitenda kazi kwa miaka ishirini ya shimo, gereza na jumba la kifalme hadi unasimama ukiwa umethibitishwa. Kuna sababu ufunuo wa kina kuliko wote ambao Mungu aliwahi kutoa haukuwa orodha ya sifa bali Nafsi; kweli hukaa ndani yetu kwa kina zaidi tunapoiona ikiishiwa.

There is a fourth gift in biographical preaching that no proposition can give: it lets the congregation watch a person change. Doctrine can tell a sinner that God transforms; a life shows it happening. The hearer who is sure he is too far gone watches Jacob the deceiver become Israel the prince, watches Peter the coward become the rock, watches Saul the persecutor become Paul the apostle — and dares to believe that the same God may not be finished with him either. A life on the page becomes a mirror and a promise at once. This is why the despairing are so often reached by biography when argument cannot touch them: they do not need to be told that grace works; they need to see it work in someone as unlikely as themselves.

Kuna zawadi ya nne katika kuhubiri kwa wasifu ambayo hakuna kauli ya kimafundisho inayoweza kuitoa: inaliwezesha kusanyiko kumtazama mtu akibadilika. Fundisho linaweza kumwambia mwenye dhambi kwamba Mungu hubadilisha; maisha yanaonyesha jambo hilo likitokea. Msikilizaji aliye na hakika kwamba amepotea mbali mno anamtazama Yakobo mdanganyifu akiwa Israeli mkuu, anamtazama Petro mwoga akiwa mwamba, anamtazama Sauli mtesaji akiwa Paulo mtume — na anathubutu kuamini kwamba Mungu yuleyule huenda hajamaliza naye pia. Maisha yaliyo ukurasani yanakuwa kioo na ahadi kwa wakati mmoja. Hii ndiyo sababu wale waliokata tamaa hufikiwa mara nyingi sana kwa wasifu wakati hoja haiwezi kuwagusa: hawahitaji kuambiwa kwamba neema hufanya kazi; wanahitaji kuiona ikifanya kazi ndani ya mtu asiyetarajiwa kama wao wenyewe.
5.3 Three Ways to Treat a Bible Character
5.3 Njia Tatu za Kumshughulikia Mhusika wa Biblia

A Bible character may be handled in three ways, and the skilled preacher chooses among them as the sermon requires. The first is to use the character as an illustration — a brief reference dropped under a point in some other sermon. You are preaching on trust, and you pause for a sentence or two to recall how Abraham left Ur not knowing where he was going. The life is not the sermon; it is a quick, bright window opened and shut to let the truth in. The second is to use the character as explanation and illustration — a fuller treatment, where the person becomes a whole movement of the message, both explaining the truth and embodying it. Here you might give ten minutes to Peter's denial and restoration to unfold the truth that Christ recovers those who fail Him. The third, and fullest, is to make the character a complete sermon — the entire message built on one life, studied and retold from beginning to end, so that the arc of the person becomes the arc of the sermon. This is the hardest of the three, and the most powerful, for it gives the preacher room to let a life live before the congregation and then to drive its truth all the way home.

Mhusika wa Biblia anaweza kushughulikiwa kwa njia tatu, na mhubiri stadi huchagua kati yake kama mahubiri yanavyohitaji. Ya kwanza ni kumtumia mhusika kama kielelezo — kumtaja kwa ufupi chini ya hoja fulani katika mahubiri mengine. Unahubiri juu ya kutumaini, na unasimama kwa sentensi moja au mbili kukumbusha jinsi Ibrahimu alivyoondoka Uru bila kujua aendako. Maisha hayo si mahubiri; ni dirisha la haraka lenye mwanga linalofunguliwa na kufungwa ili kuiingiza kweli. Ya pili ni kumtumia mhusika kama maelezo na kielelezo — kumshughulikia kwa ukamilifu zaidi, ambapo mtu huyo anakuwa sehemu nzima ya ujumbe, akiieleza kweli na pia akiiishi. Hapa unaweza kutoa dakika kumi kwa kukana kwa Petro na kurejeshwa kwake ili kufunua kweli kwamba Kristo huwarejesha wale wanaomwangusha. Ya tatu, na iliyo kamili kuliko zote, ni kumfanya mhusika kuwa mahubiri kamili — ujumbe wote ukijengwa juu ya maisha ya mtu mmoja, yakichunguzwa na kusimuliwa upya tangu mwanzo hadi mwisho, ili mkondo wa maisha ya mtu huyo uwe mkondo wa mahubiri. Hii ndiyo ngumu kuliko zote tatu, na yenye nguvu kuliko zote, kwa sababu inampa mhubiri nafasi ya kuacha maisha yaishi mbele ya kusanyiko kisha kuisukuma kweli yake hadi ifike nyumbani kabisa.

How do you choose among the three? Let the truth and the time decide. If a life merely confirms a point you are already making, keep it brief — use it as an illustration and move on, or it will swell out of proportion and capsize the sermon. If a life is rich enough to carry a major movement of the message and the hour allows, give it the fuller explanation-and-illustration treatment. And if a single life embodies the whole truth you mean to preach, and you have studied it to the depths, give it the entire sermon. The danger at every level is the same: never let the character grow larger than the truth he was summoned to serve.

Unachaguaje kati ya hizo tatu? Acha kweli na muda viamue. Ikiwa maisha fulani yanathibitisha tu hoja unayoitoa tayari, yaweke mafupi — yatumie kama kielelezo kisha endelea, la sivyo yatavimba kupita kiasi na kuyapindua mahubiri. Ikiwa maisha ni tajiri vya kutosha kubeba sehemu kubwa ya ujumbe na muda unaruhusu, yape matumizi kamili zaidi ya maelezo na kielelezo. Na ikiwa maisha ya mtu mmoja yanaiwakilisha kweli nzima unayokusudia kuhubiri, nawe umeyachunguza hadi vilindini, yape mahubiri yote. Hatari katika kila ngazi ni ileile: kamwe usimwache mhusika akue kuliko kweli aliyoitwa kuitumikia.
5.4 "Payday — Someday"
5.4 "Payday — Someday" ("Siku ya Malipo — Siku Moja")

The most famous example of the complete-sermon treatment in the American pulpit is R.G. Lee's "Payday — Someday." Lee, the longtime pastor of Bellevue Baptist Church in Memphis, built an entire sermon on the cast of 1 Kings 21 — wicked King Ahab; his ruthless queen, Jezebel; honest Naboth, who would not sell the vineyard of his fathers; and the prophet Elijah, who appears at the end with the verdict of God. Lee retells the whole grim story: the king's sulking covetousness, the queen's cold-blooded plot, the forged letters, the false witnesses, the judicial murder of an innocent man, and then the meeting in the stolen vineyard where Elijah pronounces the doom that sin has earned. The single theme runs through it like a drumbeat to its thundering refrain — that sin will surely be paid its wages: Payday — Someday.

Mfano maarufu kuliko yote wa mahubiri kamili katika mimbari ya Marekani ni "Payday — Someday" ("Siku ya Malipo — Siku Moja") ya R.G. Lee. Lee, aliyekuwa mchungaji kwa muda mrefu wa Kanisa la Kibaptisti la Bellevue huko Memphis, alijenga mahubiri mazima juu ya wahusika wa 1 Wafalme 21 — Mfalme Ahabu mwovu; malkia wake katili, Yezebeli; Nabothi mwaminifu, ambaye hakukubali kuuza shamba la mizabibu la baba zake; na nabii Eliya, anayetokea mwishoni akiwa na hukumu ya Mungu. Lee anaisimulia upya hadithi yote ya kutisha: tamaa ya mfalme aliyenuna, hila ya kikatili ya malkia, barua za kughushi, mashahidi wa uongo, mauaji ya mtu asiye na hatia kwa njia ya mahakama, kisha kukutana katika shamba la mizabibu lililoporwa ambapo Eliya anatangaza maangamizi ambayo dhambi imeyastahili. Wazo moja linapita ndani yake kama mdundo wa ngoma hadi kiitikio chake cha ngurumo — kwamba dhambi hakika italipwa mshahara wake: Payday — Someday (Siku ya Malipo — Siku Moja).

Notice what the complete-sermon form made possible. Lee did not state "sin has consequences" as point one and move on; he made the congregation stand in the vineyard, hear Jezebel's orders, watch Naboth die, and feel the ground shift when the prophet stepped from the shadows. The vivid narrative and the thundering truth were not two things but one. And there is a second lesson, half a joke and wholly instructive: Lee preached this one sermon well over a thousand times across his long ministry — to different congregations, of course. A biographical sermon that has been truly built, studied to the depths and shaped with care, does not wear out. It can be preached again and again to new hearers with its power undiminished, because the life at its center is inexhaustible and the truth it carries never ages. That is the reward of the labor the complete-sermon form demands.

Angalia kile ambacho umbo la mahubiri kamili liliwezesha. Lee hakutamka "dhambi ina matokeo" kama hoja ya kwanza kisha akaendelea; alilifanya kusanyiko lisimame shambani mwa mizabibu, lisikie amri za Yezebeli, limtazame Nabothi akifa, na kuhisi ardhi ikitikisika nabii alipotoka gizani. Simulizi lenye uhai na kweli yenye ngurumo havikuwa vitu viwili bali kimoja. Na kuna funzo la pili, nusu mzaha na lenye mafundisho kamili: Lee aliyahubiri mahubiri haya moja zaidi ya mara elfu moja katika huduma yake ndefu — kwa makusanyiko tofauti, bila shaka. Mahubiri ya wasifu yaliyojengwa kweli, yakachunguzwa hadi vilindini na kuundwa kwa uangalifu, hayachakai. Yanaweza kuhubiriwa tena na tena kwa wasikilizaji wapya bila nguvu yake kupungua, kwa sababu maisha yaliyo katikati yake hayaishi na kweli inayobebwa nayo haizeeki kamwe. Hiyo ndiyo thawabu ya kazi ambayo umbo la mahubiri kamili linadai.

One more thing the sermon teaches the preacher. For most of its length the wicked seem to win: the vineyard is seized, the innocent man is buried, the queen smiles. A lesser sermon would have rushed to reassure us; the biographical form has the patience to let the injustice stand unanswered, so that when Elijah finally steps forward, the relief and the terror of God's justice land with their full weight. The shape of the life dictates the shape of the sermon — the long silence of heaven, and then the sudden verdict. A preacher who flattens that arc into three even points throws away the very tension that makes the truth unbearable and unforgettable. Let the story's own rhythm preach.

Kuna jambo moja zaidi ambalo mahubiri haya yanamfundisha mhubiri. Kwa sehemu kubwa ya urefu wake waovu wanaonekana kushinda: shamba la mizabibu linanyakuliwa, mtu asiye na hatia anazikwa, malkia anatabasamu. Mahubiri dhaifu yangeharakisha kututuliza; umbo la wasifu lina subira ya kuuacha udhalimu usimame bila kujibiwa, ili Eliya hatimaye anapojitokeza, faraja na hofu ya haki ya Mungu vitue kwa uzito wake wote. Umbo la maisha linaamua umbo la mahubiri — ukimya mrefu wa mbinguni, kisha hukumu ya ghafla. Mhubiri anayeubana mkondo huo ukawa hoja tatu zilizo sawa hutupilia mbali mvutano uleule unaoifanya kweli isivumilike na isisahaulike. Acha mdundo wa hadithi yenyewe uhubiri.
5.5 The Craft and the Danger
5.5 Ufundi na Hatari

To preach a life well, study it the way Unit 4 taught you to study a narrative, only now with the focus held on one person. Trace his previous history and why he matters; map his relationships; ask what became of him in the end, and why; search out where else Scripture mentions him. Listen to his words, weigh his silences, mark the places and events that shaped him. Out of that patient study a clear portrait will emerge — and only a portrait you can see clearly will you be able to make others see.

Ili kuhubiri maisha ya mtu vizuri, yachunguze kwa jinsi Sehemu ya 4 ilivyokufundisha kuchunguza simulizi, ila sasa ukishikilia mkazo juu ya mtu mmoja. Fuatilia historia yake ya awali na kwa nini ana umuhimu; chora ramani ya mahusiano yake; uliza kilichompata mwishoni, na kwa nini; tafuta mahali pengine Maandiko yanapomtaja. Sikiliza maneno yake, pima ukimya wake, weka alama mahali na matukio yaliyomuunda. Kutokana na uchunguzi huo wa subira picha iliyo wazi itajitokeza — na ni picha tu unayoweza kuiona wazi ndiyo utakayoweza kuwafanya wengine waione.

How shall the complete biographical sermon be structured? Most often the life supplies its own outline. You may simply follow the arc — the rise, the turning point, the fall or the triumph, the end — and let chronology carry the hearer, as a story naturally does. Or you may gather the life around a single theme, returning to the person again and again to develop one truth his career displays. Either way, resist the urge to impose an artificial three-point grid on a life that has its own God-given shape. The man was not born, did not sin, did not repent, and did not die in alliterated installments. Study the life until its true shape appears, preach that shape, and trust the One who wrote the life to have written the sermon into it already.

Mahubiri kamili ya wasifu yapangwe vipi? Mara nyingi maisha yenyewe hutoa muhtasari wake. Unaweza kufuata tu mkondo wake — kuinuka, hatua ya mgeuko, anguko au ushindi, mwisho — na kuacha mpangilio wa wakati umbebe msikilizaji, kama hadithi inavyofanya kwa asili. Au unaweza kuyakusanya maisha kuzunguka wazo moja, ukimrudia mtu huyo tena na tena ili kuikuza kweli moja ambayo maisha yake yanaionyesha. Kwa njia yoyote ile, pinga tamaa ya kulazimisha kiunzi bandia cha hoja tatu juu ya maisha yaliyo na umbo lake alilopewa na Mungu. Mtu huyo hakuzaliwa, hakutenda dhambi, hakutubu, wala hakufa kwa vipande vyenye herufi za mwanzo zinazofanana. Yachunguze maisha hadi umbo lake la kweli lijitokeze, hubiri umbo hilo, na umtumaini Yule aliyeandika maisha hayo kuwa tayari ameyaandika mahubiri ndani yake.

But guard against the one besetting danger of this form: moralizing. It is fatally easy to reduce a biographical sermon to a flat lesson in behavior — "be brave like Daniel," "do not compromise like Lot" — as though the gospel were merely a program of self-improvement and the Bible a gallery of good and bad examples. That is not Christian preaching; it is ethics with a religious accent, and it leaves the hearer trying harder instead of trusting Christ. The cure is to let every life finally point beyond itself, to the God who shaped it and the grace that alone can save. Even a sermon of pure warning must do this. "Payday — Someday" is not finally an exhortation to be nicer than Ahab; it is a summons to flee the wrath to come and find refuge in the Savior, for if sin has a payday, then grace is the only escape. Dr. Cook's own biographical sermons hold this balance. His sermon on Felix takes the trembling Roman governor who heard Paul reason of righteousness and judgment and said, "Go thy way for this time" — and presses the peril of the convenient season that never comes. His sermon on the thief on the cross takes the dying criminal who turned to Christ in his last hour and preaches the reach of grace at the eleventh hour. His sermon on the rich young ruler takes the fine young man who came running, knelt, and walked away sorrowful — and lays bare the tragedy of the almost-saved. In each, a life is retold with care, and in each the life opens onto Christ. That is biographical preaching at its truest: not the admiration of a human being, but a meeting, through one human life, with the God who made it and the grace that redeems it. In the next unit we turn to the stories the Master Storyteller told about other people — the parables of Jesus.

Lakini jilinde dhidi ya hatari moja inayolinyemelea umbo hili daima: kuhubiri maadili tu (moralizing). Ni rahisi kwa namna ya kuangamiza kuyapunguza mahubiri ya wasifu kuwa somo tupu la tabia — "uwe jasiri kama Danieli," "usilegee kama Lutu" — kana kwamba injili ni mpango wa kujiboresha tu na Biblia ni jumba la maonyesho la mifano mizuri na mibaya. Hayo si mahubiri ya Kikristo; ni maadili yenye lafudhi ya kidini, nayo humwacha msikilizaji akijitahidi zaidi badala ya kumtumaini Kristo. Dawa ni kuacha kila maisha hatimaye yaelekeze mbele zaidi yake yenyewe, kwa Mungu aliyeyaunda na kwa neema ambayo peke yake inaweza kuokoa. Hata mahubiri ya onyo tupu lazima yafanye hivi. "Payday — Someday" mwishowe si wito wa kuwa mwema kuliko Ahabu; ni wito wa kuikimbia ghadhabu ijayo na kupata kimbilio kwa Mwokozi, kwa maana ikiwa dhambi ina siku ya malipo, basi neema ndiyo njia pekee ya kuokoka. Mahubiri ya wasifu ya Dkt. Cook mwenyewe yanashikilia uwiano huu. Mahubiri yake juu ya Feliki yanamchukua liwali wa Kirumi aliyetetemeka alipomsikia Paulo akihojiana juu ya haki na hukumu, akasema, "Enenda zako sasa; nikipata nafasi nitakuita" — na yanasisitiza hatari ya nafasi inayofaa ambayo haiji kamwe. Mahubiri yake juu ya mnyang'anyi msalabani yanamchukua mhalifu aliyekuwa akifa aliyemgeukia Kristo katika saa yake ya mwisho na kuhubiri jinsi neema inavyofika hata saa ya kumi na moja. Mahubiri yake juu ya kijana mtawala tajiri yanamchukua kijana mwema aliyekuja akipiga mbio, akapiga magoti, kisha akaondoka kwa huzuni — na yanaufunua msiba wa aliyekaribia kuokoka. Katika kila moja, maisha yanasimuliwa upya kwa uangalifu, na katika kila moja maisha yanafunguka kuelekea kwa Kristo. Huko ndiko kuhubiri kwa wasifu katika ukweli wake halisi: si kumstaajabia binadamu, bali kukutana, kupitia maisha ya binadamu mmoja, na Mungu aliyeyaumba na neema inayoyakomboa. The Parables of Jesus
Mifano ya Yesu

No one ever told stories like Jesus. The parables are the high-water mark of everything this course has taught — short, earthly tales that open onto the kingdom of heaven and that have lost none of their power in two thousand years. But they are also the most misused stories in Scripture, buried for centuries under clever interpretations that smothered the very point they were told to make. To preach them well, we must understand what a parable is, how it works on the hearer, and the long and cautionary history of how the church has read them.

Hakuna mtu aliyewahi kusimulia hadithi kama Yesu. Mifano ndiyo kilele cha yote ambayo kozi hii imefundisha — hadithi fupi za kidunia zinazofungua mlango kuelekea ufalme wa mbinguni, ambazo hazijapoteza hata chembe ya nguvu zake katika miaka elfu mbili. Lakini pia ndizo hadithi zinazotumiwa vibaya kuliko zote katika Maandiko, zilizozikwa kwa karne nyingi chini ya tafsiri za kijanja ambazo zilikaba pumzi ya jambo lenyewe zilizosimuliwa kulifundisha. Ili kuzihubiri vizuri, ni lazima tuelewe mfano ni nini, unavyofanya kazi ndani ya msikilizaji, na historia ndefu yenye maonyo ya jinsi kanisa lilivyoisoma.
6.1 The Master Storyteller
6.1 Msimulizi Mkuu

Of all the teachers who ever lived, the one with perfect knowledge of the human heart chose to teach mostly in stories. "All these things spake Jesus unto the multitude in parables; and without a parable spake he not unto them" (Matthew 13:34). He could have lectured; He could have handed down systematic propositions; instead He told of a sower scattering seed, a woman sweeping for a lost coin, a father watching a road, a man beaten and left half dead. A parable is an earthly story laid beside a heavenly truth — a comparison, which is what the word itself means: something "thrown alongside." Again and again He began, "The kingdom of heaven is like..." and then He painted a picture from the common life of His hearers — farming, fishing, baking, borrowing, a wedding, a debt — and through that homely window the light of the kingdom came pouring in.

Kati ya walimu wote waliowahi kuishi, Yule mwenye ujuzi kamili wa moyo wa mwanadamu alichagua kufundisha zaidi kwa hadithi. "Hayo yote Yesu aliwaambia makutano kwa mifano, wala pasipo mfano hakuwaambia neno" (Mathayo 13:34). Angeweza kutoa mihadhara; angeweza kutoa kauli za kimfumo; badala yake alisimulia habari ya mpanzi akitawanya mbegu, mwanamke akifagia nyumba akitafuta shilingi iliyopotea, baba akiitazama njia, mtu aliyepigwa na kuachwa karibu kufa. Mfano ni hadithi ya kidunia iliyowekwa kando ya kweli ya kimbingu — ulinganisho, na hiyo ndiyo maana ya neno lenyewe: kitu "kilichotupwa kando" ya kingine. Tena na tena alianza, "Ufalme wa mbinguni umefanana na..." kisha akachora picha kutoka maisha ya kawaida ya wasikilizaji wake — kilimo, uvuvi, kuoka mkate, kukopa, harusi, deni — na kupitia dirisha hilo la nyumbani nuru ya ufalme ikaingia kwa wingi.

For the preacher, this settles the matter that Unit 1 first raised. If the Lord Himself, with all of heaven's truth to deliver, made the story His chief method, then the story is no lightweight compromise. It is the very tool the Master reached for. Everything in this course finds its model here: the parables are the story sermon in its perfection.

Kwa mhubiri, jambo hili linamaliza swali lililoulizwa kwanza katika Sehemu ya 1. Ikiwa Bwana Mwenyewe, akiwa na kweli yote ya mbinguni ya kutoa, aliifanya hadithi kuwa njia yake kuu, basi hadithi si mapatano mepesi. Ndicho chombo hasa ambacho Bwana alikinyooshea mkono. Kila kitu katika kozi hii kinapata kielelezo chake hapa: mifano ndiyo mahubiri ya masimulizi katika ukamilifu wake.

There is a deeper mystery in Jesus' use of parables, and the preacher should know it. When the disciples asked why He spoke in parables, He answered that the stories both reveal and conceal: to the humble and hungry they open the kingdom, but to the proud and hard-hearted they remain a riddle — "that seeing they may see, and not perceive" (Mark 4:12, echoing Isaiah 6). The parable is a kind of sieve. The same story that melts a soft heart hardens a resistant one, because the truth it carries must be received, not merely overheard, and the man who will not bend to it is left holding only a charming tale about seeds or sheep. This should sober the preacher: a story is not a magic trick that compels belief. It lays the truth before the will, and waits.

Kuna siri ya ndani zaidi katika jinsi Yesu alivyotumia mifano, na mhubiri anapaswa kuijua. Wanafunzi walipomwuliza kwa nini alisema kwa mifano, alijibu kwamba hadithi hizo hufunua na pia huficha: kwa wanyenyekevu na wenye njaa huufungua ufalme, lakini kwa wenye kiburi na mioyo migumu hubaki kitendawili — "ili wakitazama watazame wasione" (Marko 4:12, ikirudia Isaya 6). Mfano ni aina ya chekecheke. Hadithi ile ile inayoyeyusha moyo laini huufanya mgumu moyo unaopinga, kwa sababu kweli inayobebwa nayo lazima ipokelewe, si kusikiwa tu kwa bahati, na mtu asiyetaka kuinama mbele yake anabaki ameshika hadithi nzuri tu kuhusu mbegu au kondoo. Jambo hili linapaswa kumtia mhubiri kiasi: hadithi si mchezo wa kiinimacho unaolazimisha mtu aamini. Inaiweka kweli mbele ya nia ya mtu, kisha inasubiri.
6.2 One Story, One Point
6.2 Hadithi Moja, Hoja Moja

Here is the first rule, and the most often broken: a parable usually makes one central point. It is a comparison, and a comparison has one main thing it compares. The parable is not, as a rule, an allegory in which every detail conceals a separate hidden meaning. This sounds obvious, yet for most of church history it was forgotten, and the parables were treated as elaborate codes to be cracked. The famous example is the Good Samaritan. Augustine read it as a vast allegory: the wounded traveler is Adam, fallen; Jerusalem is the heavenly city he left; the robbers are the devil and his angels; the priest and Levite are the old covenant, unable to save; the Samaritan is Christ; the inn is the church; the innkeeper is the apostle Paul; the two coins are the two sacraments. It is ingenious, and it is almost entirely beside the point — for Jesus told that story to answer one question, "Who is my neighbour?", and to drive home one truth: go and be the neighbor, even to the man you despise. The allegory was so busy decoding the inn and the coins that it buried the thunderclap Jesus actually aimed at the lawyer's heart.

Hii ndiyo kanuni ya kwanza, na ndiyo inayovunjwa mara nyingi zaidi: kwa kawaida mfano hutoa hoja moja kuu. Ni ulinganisho, na ulinganisho una jambo moja kuu unalolinganisha. Kwa kawaida mfano si istiari (allegory) ambamo kila undani huficha maana yake ya siri. Jambo hili linaonekana wazi, lakini kwa muda mrefu wa historia ya kanisa lilisahauliwa, na mifano ilichukuliwa kama misimbo tata ya kufumbuliwa. Mfano maarufu ni ule wa Msamaria Mwema. Augustino aliusoma kama istiari kubwa: msafiri aliyejeruhiwa ni Adamu aliyeanguka; Yerusalemu ni mji wa mbinguni aliouacha; wanyang'anyi ni Ibilisi na malaika zake; kuhani na Mlawi ni agano la kale, lisiloweza kuokoa; Msamaria ni Kristo; nyumba ya wageni ni kanisa; mwenye nyumba ya wageni ni mtume Paulo; dinari mbili ni sakramenti mbili. Ni ubunifu wa ajabu, nao karibu wote uko nje kabisa ya hoja — kwa maana Yesu alisimulia hadithi ile kujibu swali moja, "Na jirani yangu ni nani?", na kusisitiza kweli moja: nenda ukawe jirani, hata kwa mtu unayemdharau. Istiari ile ilishughulika mno kufumbua nyumba ya wageni na dinari hata ikazika radi ambayo Yesu hasa aliilenga moyoni mwa yule mwana-sheria.

So the working rule for the preacher is this: find the one main point, the single comparison the parable was told to make, and preach that. Do not go hunting for a secret significance in the color of the donkey or the number of the coins. Ask instead, "What one truth did Jesus drive home with this story?" — and let that truth be your sermon.

Kwa hiyo kanuni ya kazi kwa mhubiri ni hii: tafuta hoja moja kuu, ulinganisho mmoja ambao mfano ulisimuliwa kuutoa, na uhubiri huo. Usiende kuwinda maana ya siri katika rangi ya punda au idadi ya dinari. Uliza badala yake, "Ni kweli gani moja ambayo Yesu aliisisitiza kwa hadithi hii?" — na kweli hiyo iwe mahubiri yako.

How do you find the one point? Look first at the frame. Often the Gospel writer, or Jesus Himself, tells you plainly why the story was told: Luke says the parable of the persistent widow was given so that men "ought always to pray, and not to faint" (Luke 18:1); the parable of the Pharisee and the publican was spoken to certain ones "which trusted in themselves that they were righteous" (Luke 18:9). The setting, the question that prompted the story, and the comment that follows it are your surest guides to its single thrust. When the text hands you the point, take it gratefully, and do not go looking for a cleverer one of your own.

Unaipataje hoja hiyo moja? Angalia kwanza kiunzi chake. Mara nyingi mwandishi wa Injili, au Yesu Mwenyewe, anakuambia waziwazi kwa nini hadithi ilisimuliwa: Luka anasema mfano wa mjane mwenye kusisitiza ulitolewa ili kwamba "imewapasa kumwomba Mungu siku zote, wala wasikate tamaa" (Luka 18:1); mfano wa Farisayo na mtoza ushuru ulinenwa kwa watu fulani "waliojikinai ya kuwa wao ni wenye haki" (Luka 18:9). Mazingira, swali lililoizaa hadithi, na maneno yanayoifuata ndiyo viongozi wako wa hakika zaidi kuelekea msukumo wake mmoja. Maandiko yanapokukabidhi hoja, ipokee kwa shukrani, wala usiende kutafuta nyingine ya kijanja zaidi ya kwako mwenyewe.
6.3 The Sting in the Tail
6.3 Mwiba Mkiani

The parables are the purest inductive preaching in the Bible (remember Unit 3). They do not announce their point at the front door; they draw the hearer in, get him to take sides, and then spring a trap. Jesus' stories are full of a sudden reversal — a sting in the tail — that catches the listener exactly where he is proud. The man who asked "Who is my neighbour?" surely expected the hero to be a priest; the hero turns out to be a Samaritan, the very people he despised. The respectable crowd listening to the Pharisee and the publican knew which man God favored — and the parable sends the tax collector home justified and the proud man empty. The Pharisees grumbling that Jesus received sinners (Luke 15:2) were invited to enjoy a story about a lost boy come home — and then the elder brother stepped onto the stage, sour and self-righteous, refusing to go in to the feast, and every grumbler in the audience was looking into a mirror.

Mifano ndiyo mahubiri safi kabisa ya kiinduktivu katika Biblia (kumbuka Sehemu ya 3). Haitangazi hoja yao mlangoni; humvuta msikilizaji ndani, humfanya achague upande, kisha hufyatua mtego. Hadithi za Yesu zimejaa mgeuko wa ghafla — mwiba mkiani — unaomkamata msikilizaji hasa pale anapojivuna. Mtu aliyeuliza "Na jirani yangu ni nani?" bila shaka alitarajia shujaa awe kuhani; shujaa anageuka kuwa Msamaria, watu wale wale aliowadharau. Umati wa watu wa heshima uliokuwa ukisikiliza habari ya Farisayo na mtoza ushuru ulijua ni yupi Mungu alimpendelea — na mfano unamrudisha nyumbani mtoza ushuru akiwa amehesabiwa haki na yule mwenye kiburi mikono mitupu. Mafarisayo waliokuwa wakinung'unika kwamba Yesu huwakaribisha wenye dhambi (Luka 15:2) walialikwa kufurahia hadithi ya mvulana aliyepotea na kurudi nyumbani — kisha kaka mkubwa akapanda jukwaani, mwenye uchungu na mwenye kujiona mwenye haki, akikataa kuingia karamuni, na kila mnung'unikaji katika umati akawa anajitazama kwenye kioo.

This is Nathan's "Thou art the man" made into an art form. And it tells the preacher how a parable must be handled in the pulpit: you must preserve the surprise. If you announce the ending before you tell the story — "Here is a parable about how we should love even our enemies" — you have disarmed the trap before it can close. Let the story do its work. Let the hearer ride along, judging the characters, sure of himself — and then let the sting land. A parable explained in advance is a parable defused, and a defused parable saves no one.

Huu ndio "Wewe ndiwe mtu huyo" wa Nathani uliogeuzwa kuwa sanaa. Na unamwambia mhubiri jinsi mfano unavyopaswa kushughulikiwa mimbarini: ni lazima uhifadhi mshangao. Ukitangaza mwisho kabla ya kusimulia hadithi — "Huu ni mfano kuhusu jinsi tunavyopaswa kuwapenda hata adui zetu" — umeutegua mtego kabla haujafunga. Iache hadithi ifanye kazi yake. Mwache msikilizaji asafiri nayo, akiwahukumu wahusika, akiwa na uhakika wa nafsi yake — kisha mwiba ugonge. Mfano ulioelezwa mapema ni mfano ulioteguliwa, na mfano ulioteguliwa haumwokoi mtu yeyote.

The reversals are everywhere once you look. The laborers hired at the eleventh hour are paid as much as those who bore the heat of the whole day, and the early workers' grumbling is our grumbling at a grace that seems unfair. The rich man who pulls down his barns to build bigger ones, congratulating himself on a comfortable future, hears in the night, "Thou fool, this night thy soul shall be required of thee." The wedding guest who scrambles for the best seat is shamed before the whole table. In every case the hearer is first invited to agree with the wrong instinct — to envy, to hoard, to grasp at honor — and then the story turns and exposes that instinct as deadly. The parable does not argue the hearer out of his sin; it lets him watch himself in it and recoil.

Migeuko hii iko kila mahali ukishaanza kutazama. Vibarua walioajiriwa saa ya kumi na moja wanalipwa sawa na wale waliostahimili jua kali la siku nzima, na manung'uniko ya wafanyakazi wa mapema ndiyo manung'uniko yetu dhidi ya neema inayoonekana kuwa si ya haki. Tajiri anayebomoa ghala zake ili ajenge kubwa zaidi, akijipongeza kwa maisha ya raha yajayo, anasikia usiku, "Mpumbavu wewe, usiku huu wanataka roho yako." Mgeni wa harusini anayegombea kiti bora anaaibishwa mbele ya meza nzima. Katika kila tukio msikilizaji kwanza anaalikwa kukubaliana na silika iliyo potofu — kuona wivu, kujilimbikizia mali, kunyakua heshima — kisha hadithi inageuka na kuifunua silika hiyo kuwa ya mauti. Mfano haumshawishi msikilizaji kwa hoja atoke katika dhambi yake; unamwacha ajitazame akiwa ndani yake, naye aogope na kurudi nyuma.
6.4 A Cautionary History
6.4 Historia Yenye Onyo

It is worth knowing how the church arrived at the one-point rule, because the story guards us from two errors at once. For the first eighteen centuries, allegory reigned: the fathers and the medieval church mined every parable for hidden correspondences, and the Samaritan's inn became the church, his oil and wine the sacraments, and so on through every detail. Then, near the end of the nineteenth century, the German scholar Adolf Jülicher reacted hard against all of it, insisting that a parable makes a single point of comparison and is not an allegory at all. The corrective was needed and largely right, and it rescued the parables from the code-breakers. In the twentieth century C.H. Dodd and Joachim Jeremias carried the work further, setting the parables back into their original soil — the ministry of Jesus, the in-breaking of the kingdom of God, the crisis facing those who first heard them — so that we read them not as timeless moral fables but as words spoken into a real and urgent moment. More recently still, scholars have recovered the sense that a parable is not merely an illustration of a truth but an event that happens to the hearer: it does something to him, draws him in, and changes him. Patrick Willson speaks of preaching along the parable's "trajectory" — aiming it so that it does to the modern congregation what it did to the first, springing the same trap in a new room.

Inafaa kujua jinsi kanisa lilivyofikia kanuni ya hoja moja, kwa sababu historia hiyo inatulinda dhidi ya makosa mawili kwa wakati mmoja. Kwa karne kumi na nane za kwanza, istiari ilitawala: mababa wa kanisa na kanisa la zama za kati walichimba kila mfano wakitafuta mawiano yaliyofichika, na nyumba ya wageni ya Msamaria ikawa kanisa, mafuta na divai yake sakramenti, na kadhalika katika kila undani. Kisha, karibu na mwisho wa karne ya kumi na tisa, mwanazuoni Mjerumani Adolf Jülicher aliyapinga kwa nguvu yote hayo, akisisitiza kwamba mfano hutoa hoja moja ya ulinganisho na si istiari hata kidogo. Marekebisho hayo yalihitajika na kwa kiasi kikubwa yalikuwa sahihi, nayo yaliiokoa mifano mikononi mwa wafumbuzi wa misimbo. Katika karne ya ishirini C.H. Dodd na Joachim Jeremias waliendeleza kazi hiyo, wakiirudisha mifano katika udongo wake wa asili — huduma ya Yesu, kuingia kwa nguvu kwa ufalme wa Mungu, hali ya dharura iliyowakabili wale walioisikia kwanza — ili tuisome si kama hadithi za maadili zisizo na wakati bali kama maneno yaliyonenwa katika saa halisi na ya dharura. Hivi karibuni zaidi, wanazuoni wamerudisha ufahamu kwamba mfano si kielelezo tu cha kweli fulani bali ni tukio linalompata msikilizaji: unamtendea jambo, unamvuta ndani, na kumbadilisha. Patrick Willson anazungumza juu ya kuhubiri kufuata "mwelekeo wa mruko" (trajectory) wa mfano — kuulenga ili uwatendee waumini wa leo kile ulichowatendea wa kwanza, ukifyatua mtego ule ule katika chumba kipya.

Yet here a balancing word is needed, for Jülicher may be pressed too far. Jesus Himself did not always hold to a single point: He interpreted the Parable of the Sower detail by detail (the seed, the path, the rocky ground, the thorns, the good soil), and He did the same with the Wheat and the Tares. Some parables, then, do carry interpreted elements, given to us by the Lord's own authority. So the rule is a wise guard, not an iron law. Resist the old itch to turn every detail into a cipher — but do not deny the meanings Jesus Himself assigned. Seek the central thrust; honor the interpretations He gave; and let the rest of the details simply furnish the story.

Lakini hapa neno la kusawazisha linahitajika, kwa maana Jülicher anaweza kusukumwa mbali mno. Yesu Mwenyewe hakushikilia hoja moja peke yake kila mara: aliufafanua Mfano wa Mpanzi undani kwa undani (mbegu, njia, penye mwamba, miiba, udongo mzuri), na akafanya vivyo hivyo kwa Ngano na Magugu. Basi baadhi ya mifano kweli ina vipengele vilivyofafanuliwa, tulivyopewa kwa mamlaka ya Bwana Mwenyewe. Kwa hiyo kanuni hii ni kinga ya hekima, si sheria ya chuma. Pinga hamu ya zamani ya kugeuza kila undani kuwa msimbo — lakini usikane maana ambazo Yesu Mwenyewe alizitoa. Tafuta msukumo mkuu; heshimu tafsiri alizozitoa; na viache vipengele vingine vipambe hadithi tu.

One last caution as you prepare to preach them. Because the parables are so familiar, your hearers think they already know them, and familiarity has dulled the very edge that once cut. Part of your task is to make the old story strange again — to recover the shock the first audience felt, when "a certain Samaritan" was not a Sunday-school hero but a hated heretic, and a tax collector was not a sympathetic figure but a traitor grown rich on his neighbors' misery. Strip away the stained-glass glow, set the story back in its original scandal, and let your congregation feel for the first time what it cost to hear it. A parable rescued from over-familiarity can wound and heal as sharply as the day it was first told.

Onyo moja la mwisho unapojiandaa kuihubiri. Kwa sababu mifano inajulikana sana, wasikilizaji wako wanadhani tayari wanaijua, na mazoea yameufanya butu ule ukali uliokata zamani. Sehemu ya kazi yako ni kuifanya hadithi ya zamani iwe ngeni tena — kurudisha mshtuko ambao wasikilizaji wa kwanza waliuhisi, wakati "Msamaria mmoja" hakuwa shujaa wa shule ya Jumapili bali mzushi aliyechukiwa, na mtoza ushuru hakuwa mtu wa kuonewa huruma bali msaliti aliyetajirika kwa taabu ya majirani zake. Ondoa mng'ao wa vioo vya rangi kanisani, irudishe hadithi katika kashfa yake ya asili, na waache waumini wako wahisi kwa mara ya kwanza ilivyogharimu kuisikia. Mfano uliookolewa kutoka kwenye mazoea ya kupita kiasi unaweza kujeruhi na kuponya kwa ukali ule ule wa siku ulipotolewa mara ya kwanza.
6.5 Preaching the Parables
6.5 Kuhubiri Mifano

Draw it all together into practice. First, tell the parable as a story; do not grind it into an abstract proposition and serve the powder instead of the fruit. Second, preserve the surprise — withhold the sting so that it can still strike. Third, find and preach the one central point, the comparison Jesus made, resisting the temptation to allegorize what He did not while honoring what He did. Fourth, aim the trajectory at the people in front of you, so that the parable catches your hearers in their pride exactly as it caught the lawyer, the Pharisee, and the elder brother — not a museum piece to be admired, but a living word that finds them in their seats. And fifth, keep it anchored: the parable serves the kingdom truth the Lord told it to convey, and the preacher who keeps it tied to that truth will never reduce these holy stories to mere entertainment. Handle them this way, and you will find the parables doing in your congregation what they have done for two thousand years — slipping past the defenses, springing the trap, and leaving the hearer face to face with the kingdom of God. In the next unit we move from the great stories that are the sermon to the smaller story that lives inside the sermon — the craft and the ethics of the illustration.

Kusanya yote haya kuwa vitendo. Kwanza, usimulie mfano kama hadithi; usiusage kuwa kauli dhahania na kuwapa watu unga badala ya tunda. Pili, hifadhi mshangao — zuia mwiba ili bado uweze kuchoma. Tatu, tafuta na uhubiri hoja moja kuu, ulinganisho alioufanya Yesu, ukipinga kishawishi cha kufanya istiari pale ambapo Yeye hakufanya, huku ukiheshimu pale alipofanya. Nne, ulenge mwelekeo wa mruko kwa watu walio mbele yako, ili mfano uwakamate wasikilizaji wako katika kiburi chao kama ulivyomkamata mwana-sheria, Farisayo, na kaka mkubwa — si kitu cha makumbusho cha kustaajabiwa, bali neno hai linalowakuta vitini mwao. Na tano, uushike mahali pake: mfano unatumikia kweli ya ufalme ambayo Bwana aliusimulia kuifikisha, na mhubiri anayeufunga kwenye kweli hiyo hatazishusha kamwe hadithi hizi takatifu kuwa burudani tu. Zishughulikie hivi, nawe utaona mifano ikifanya katika kusanyiko lako kile ambacho imefanya kwa miaka elfu mbili — ikipenya ngome za ulinzi, ikifyatua mtego, na kumwacha msikilizaji uso kwa uso na ufalme wa Mungu. Katika sehemu inayofuata tunatoka kwenye hadithi kubwa ambazo ndizo mahubiri kwenda kwenye hadithi ndogo inayoishi ndani ya mahubiri — ufundi na maadili ya kielelezo.
