Unit Seven · The Story Within
Sehemu ya Saba · Hadithi Iliyo Ndani
Story Inside the Sermon
Hadithi Ndani ya Mahubiri

Until now the story has been the sermon. In this unit we consider the smaller story that lives inside a sermon — the illustration. It is by far the most common use of story in preaching: every week, in pulpits that would never attempt a full story sermon, a preacher pauses to tell a tale that throws light on his point. The illustration has its own craft of finding and filing, its own range of types, and — above all — its own ethics, for nowhere is a preacher more tempted to dishonesty than in the stories he tells.

Hadi sasa hadithi imekuwa ndiyo mahubiri. Katika sehemu hii tunaitafakari hadithi ndogo inayoishi ndani ya mahubiri — kielelezo. Hii ndiyo njia inayotumika zaidi kuliko zote ya kutumia hadithi katika kuhubiri: kila wiki, katika mimbari ambazo hazingethubutu kamwe kuhubiri mahubiri kamili ya masimulizi, mhubiri husimama kidogo kusimulia kisa kinachoangaza hoja yake. Kielelezo kina ufundi wake wa kutafuta na kuhifadhi, aina zake mbalimbali, na — zaidi ya yote — maadili yake, kwa maana hakuna mahali ambapo mhubiri hujaribiwa zaidi kukosa uaminifu kuliko katika hadithi anazosimulia.
7.1 Windows in the Wall
7.1 Madirisha Ukutani

The old word is the best definition. To illustrate is to throw light upon something, and Spurgeon gave us the picture that has never been bettered: illustrations are windows in the wall of the sermon. The argument is the structure — the stone and timber of exposition and proof — but a building of solid wall is a dark place to sit. The window lets in the light, so that the truth already standing there can suddenly be seen. This is what the illustration does: it makes the abstract concrete, it rests the hearer who has been following hard reasoning, it fixes the point in the memory, and it moves the will by letting a man feel what he has only understood.

Neno la zamani ndilo fasili bora. Kuelezea kwa kielelezo ni kutupa nuru juu ya jambo, na Spurgeon alitupa picha ambayo haijawahi kuzidiwa: vielelezo ni madirisha katika ukuta wa mahubiri. Hoja ndiyo muundo — mawe na mbao za ufafanuzi na uthibitisho — lakini jengo lenye ukuta mtupu ni mahali penye giza pa kuketi. Dirisha huingiza nuru, ili kweli iliyokwisha kusimama pale ionekane ghafla. Hivi ndivyo kielelezo kinavyofanya: kinalifanya jambo dhahania kuwa halisi, kinampumzisha msikilizaji aliyekuwa akifuata hoja ngumu, kinaikaza hoja kumbukumbuni, na kinaigusa nia kwa kumwacha mtu ahisi kile ambacho alikuwa amekielewa tu.

Notice how this differs from the story sermon of the last four units. There the story was the message; it carried the whole weight. Here the story is a servant inside a larger structure, most often the deductive sermon of Unit 3: the point is stated, and then the illustration is brought in to make it vivid and believable. The window is not the house, and the illustration is not the sermon. It exists to serve the point — and the moment it forgets that, it becomes a problem rather than a help.

Angalia jinsi hili linavyotofautiana na mahubiri ya masimulizi ya sehemu nne zilizopita. Kule hadithi ilikuwa ndiyo ujumbe; ilibeba uzito wote. Hapa hadithi ni mtumishi ndani ya muundo mkubwa zaidi, mara nyingi zaidi mahubiri ya kideduktivu ya Sehemu ya 3: hoja inatajwa, kisha kielelezo kinaletwa ili kuifanya iwe hai na ya kuaminika. Dirisha si nyumba, na kielelezo si mahubiri. Kipo ili kutumikia hoja — na mara kinaposahau jambo hilo, kinakuwa tatizo badala ya msaada.

A sermon with no windows at all is its own kind of failure. You have heard such sermons — accurate, well-organized, doctrinally sound, and almost impossible to stay awake under, because the mind can hold only so much unrelieved argument before it slips its mooring and drifts. The illustration is not a concession to weak listeners; it is a mercy built into the way God made the mind. Even the strongest hearer needs the moment of rest a story gives, the moment when the eyes refocus and the heart catches up to the head. And what is rested is also persuaded: a man may grant your argument and still not move, but show him the truth living in a story and his will is engaged where his reason alone could not reach it. The window does not weaken the wall; it makes the house fit to live in.

Mahubiri yasiyo na dirisha hata moja ni kushindwa kwa aina yake. Umewahi kusikia mahubiri kama hayo — sahihi, yaliyopangwa vizuri, yenye mafundisho safi, na karibu haiwezekani kukaa macho chini yake, kwa sababu akili inaweza kubeba hoja isiyopumzishwa kwa kiasi fulani tu kabla haijakatika kamba yake na kuelea mbali. Kielelezo si kuwaridhia wasikilizaji dhaifu; ni rehema iliyojengwa ndani ya jinsi Mungu alivyoiumba akili. Hata msikilizaji hodari zaidi anahitaji kipindi cha pumziko ambacho hadithi hutoa, kipindi ambacho macho yanarudi kuona sawasawa na moyo unaifikia akili. Na kile kinachopumzishwa pia kinashawishiwa: mtu anaweza kuikubali hoja yako na bado asiguswe, lakini mwonyeshe kweli ikiishi ndani ya hadithi na nia yake inaguswa pale ambapo akili peke yake isingeweza kufika. Dirisha haliudhoofishi ukuta; linaifanya nyumba ifae kuishi ndani yake.
7.2 Finding and Filing
7.2 Kutafuta na Kuhifadhi

Where do illustrations come from? Everywhere — for the preacher who lives with his eyes open. They are in the Scriptures, in history, in the lives of great men and women, in nature and the sciences, in the day's news, in literature, and in the ordinary traffic of his own days. The preacher who complains that he can never find a good illustration is usually a preacher who walks through the world asleep. The man whose eyes are open sees a sermon in a sparrow, a parable in a traffic jam, a doctrine pictured in the way water finds its level. The illustrations are all around you; the art is to notice them.

Vielelezo vinatoka wapi? Kila mahali — kwa mhubiri anayeishi macho yake yakiwa wazi. Vimo katika Maandiko, katika historia, katika maisha ya wanaume na wanawake mashuhuri, katika maumbile na sayansi, katika habari za siku, katika fasihi, na katika shughuli za kawaida za siku zake mwenyewe. Mhubiri anayelalamika kwamba hawezi kamwe kupata kielelezo kizuri kwa kawaida ni mhubiri anayetembea duniani akiwa amelala. Mtu mwenye macho yaliyo wazi huona mahubiri katika shomoro, mfano katika msongamano wa magari, fundisho likiwa limechorwa katika jinsi maji yanavyotafuta usawa wake. Vielelezo viko kila upande wako; ufundi ni kuvitambua.

But what is noticed and not captured is lost by Saturday. The disciplined preacher therefore keeps a system — a file of cards, a notebook, a folder on his tablet — into which every good illustration goes the moment he meets it, marked with its point and its source. Over the years that file becomes a treasury, and it is precisely the treasury that the controlling-story sermon of Unit 3 draws upon. Recall that we said the controlling-story form most rewards the preacher who has spent years quietly gathering good and truthful stories. This is where that gathering happens. Begin your file today; in twenty years you will preach out of its riches, and you will never again stand empty-handed before a text.

Lakini kinachotambuliwa na kutokamatwa hupotea kabla ya Jumamosi. Kwa hiyo mhubiri mwenye nidhamu huwa na mfumo — faili la kadi, daftari, folda kwenye kishkwambi chake — ambamo kila kielelezo kizuri huingia mara anapokikuta, kikiwa kimeandikwa hoja yake na chanzo chake. Kwa miaka mingi faili hilo linakuwa hazina, na ni hazina hiyo hasa ambayo mahubiri ya hadithi-tawala ya Sehemu ya 3 huichota. Kumbuka tulisema kwamba mtindo wa hadithi-tawala humzawadia zaidi mhubiri aliyetumia miaka mingi akikusanya kimya kimya hadithi nzuri na za kweli. Huku ndiko ukusanyaji huo unakofanyika. Anza faili lako leo; baada ya miaka ishirini utahubiri kutoka katika utajiri wake, wala hutasimama tena mikono mitupu mbele ya kifungu.
7.3 The Ten Types
7.3 Aina Kumi

Illustrations come in many kinds, and it helps to know the family. We may name ten. The personal experience, drawn from the preacher's own life; the biblical, one Scripture lighting up another; the historical, an event from the human record; the biographical, a moment from a single life (the craft of Unit 5 in miniature); the natural and scientific, a truth pictured in the created order; the current event, taken from the day's news; the literary or quoted, a line from a poem, a hymn, or a wise man; the hypothetical, the "suppose a man..." that invents a case to test a truth; the analogy or figure, "the kingdom is like..." in small; and the humorous, the touch of laughter that opens a closed face. Each has its strength and its snare. The personal-experience story is the most intimate and powerful of all — nothing reaches a congregation like "let me tell you what happened to me" — but it carries the sharpest danger of self-display, of making the preacher the hero of every tale until the sermon is about him and not his Lord. Humor, likewise, can open a heart in a single sentence, but it must serve the truth and never mock the sacred, never wound a person present, and never swell until the people came for a comedian and went home without a word from God. Use all ten; master the cautions of each.

Vielelezo huja kwa aina nyingi, na inasaidia kuijua familia yake. Tunaweza kutaja kumi. Uzoefu binafsi, unaotoka katika maisha ya mhubiri mwenyewe; cha kibiblia, Maandiko yakiangaza Maandiko mengine; cha kihistoria, tukio kutoka kumbukumbu za wanadamu; cha wasifu, kipindi kutoka katika maisha ya mtu mmoja (ufundi wa Sehemu ya 5 kwa udogo); cha maumbile na sayansi, kweli iliyochorwa katika mpangilio wa uumbaji; cha tukio la sasa, kinachotoka katika habari za siku; cha fasihi au nukuu, mstari kutoka shairi, wimbo wa kiroho, au mtu mwenye hekima; cha kudhania, kile "tuseme mtu fulani..." kinachobuni kisa ili kupima kweli; cha mlinganisho au taswira, "ufalme umefanana na..." kwa udogo; na cha ucheshi, mguso wa kicheko unaofungua uso uliofungwa. Kila kimoja kina nguvu yake na mtego wake. Hadithi ya uzoefu binafsi ndiyo ya karibu zaidi na yenye nguvu kuliko zote — hakuna kinachowafikia waumini kama "ngoja nikuambie kilichonipata" — lakini ina hatari kali zaidi ya kujionyesha, ya kumfanya mhubiri kuwa shujaa wa kila kisa hadi mahubiri yanakuwa juu yake na si juu ya Bwana wake. Vivyo hivyo ucheshi unaweza kufungua moyo kwa sentensi moja, lakini lazima utumikie kweli na kamwe usidhihaki kilicho kitakatifu, kamwe usimjeruhi mtu aliyepo, na kamwe usivimbe hadi watu wanakuja kwa ajili ya mchekeshaji na kurudi nyumbani bila neno kutoka kwa Mungu. Tumia zote kumi; zijue vizuri tahadhari za kila moja.

A word on three more of the ten, for each has a trap worth naming. The current-event illustration is vivid because it is fresh, but it spoils fast; what everyone is talking about this month will be a puzzle in five years, so use it and let it go, and do not build a permanent sermon on a passing headline. The literary or quoted illustration lends weight and beauty, but it tempts a man to show his learning; a poem quoted to serve the truth is a gift, a poem quoted to display the preacher is a vanity, and the congregation can always tell the difference. The hypothetical — the honest "suppose a man..." — is a fine tool for testing a principle, but it must always wear its "suppose" openly, for the instant a hearer thinks an invented case really happened, you have crossed from illustration into deception.

Neno juu ya aina tatu zaidi kati ya hizo kumi, kwa maana kila moja ina mtego unaostahili kutajwa. Kielelezo cha tukio la sasa ni hai kwa sababu ni kipya, lakini kinaharibika upesi; kile ambacho kila mtu anakizungumza mwezi huu kitakuwa fumbo baada ya miaka mitano, kwa hiyo kitumie kisha kiache, wala usijenge mahubiri ya kudumu juu ya kichwa cha habari kinachopita. Kielelezo cha fasihi au nukuu huongeza uzito na uzuri, lakini humjaribu mtu aonyeshe elimu yake; shairi linalonukuliwa ili kutumikia kweli ni zawadi, shairi linalonukuliwa ili kumwonyesha mhubiri ni ubatili, na waumini daima wanaweza kutambua tofauti. Kielelezo cha kudhania — kile "tuseme mtu fulani..." cha uaminifu — ni chombo kizuri cha kupima kanuni, lakini lazima sikuzote kivae "tuseme" chake waziwazi, kwa maana mara msikilizaji anapodhani kwamba kisa kilichobuniwa kilitokea kweli, umevuka kutoka kielelezo kuingia udanganyifu.
7.4 The Ethics of the Borrowed Story
7.4 Maadili ya Hadithi ya Kuazima

Now to the heart of this unit, and to the place where preachers most often fall. The single greatest danger in using illustrations is not telling them badly; it is telling them dishonestly. The temptation is constant and subtle: you read a moving story of something that happened to another man, and when you tell it from the pulpit it is so much more powerful in the first person — "I was driving home one night..." — that the borrowed coat slips on almost without a decision. Robert Hastings named this preacher exactly: the "clothesline preacher," who hangs out other men's washing as if it were his own. It is a form of lying, and it is pulpit plagiarism, and a man who will steal a story to move a crowd has already begun to trade his integrity for effect.

Sasa tunafika kiini cha sehemu hii, mahali ambapo wahubiri huanguka mara nyingi zaidi. Hatari kubwa kuliko zote katika kutumia vielelezo si kuvisimulia vibaya; ni kuvisimulia bila uaminifu. Kishawishi ni cha kudumu na cha hila: unasoma hadithi inayogusa moyo ya jambo lililompata mtu mwingine, na unapoisimulia mimbarini ina nguvu zaidi sana katika nafsi ya kwanza — "Nilikuwa nikiendesha gari kurudi nyumbani usiku mmoja..." — kiasi kwamba koti la kuazima linavaliwa karibu bila uamuzi wowote. Robert Hastings alimtaja mhubiri huyu kwa usahihi kabisa: "mhubiri wa kamba ya kuanikia nguo," anayeanika nguo za watu wengine kana kwamba ni zake. Ni aina ya uongo, ni wizi wa maandishi mimbarini, na mtu atakayeiba hadithi ili kuugusa umati amekwisha kuanza kubadilishana uadilifu wake kwa matokeo.

The remedy is simple, and costs only a little pride: credit your sources honestly. You lose almost nothing by saying "I read of a man who..." or "a friend once told me..." — and you keep everything that matters, your own truthfulness and the trust of your people. Dr. Cook's own practice is the model. Two illustrations he has carried for years are set down here in full, each told under the name it wears — the first a gift from a friend, the second handed down through a long chain of preachers — so you may see that a borrowed story loses none of its power when the borrowing is owned aloud.

Dawa ni rahisi, na inagharimu kiburi kidogo tu: taja vyanzo vyako kwa uaminifu. Hupotezi karibu kitu chochote kwa kusema "Nilisoma habari ya mtu mmoja aliye..." au "rafiki aliwahi kuniambia..." — nawe unabaki na kila kitu chenye maana, uaminifu wako mwenyewe na imani ya watu wako kwako. Utendaji wa Dkt. Cook mwenyewe ndio kielelezo. Vielelezo viwili ambavyo amevibeba kwa miaka mingi vimeandikwa hapa kikamilifu, kila kimoja kikisimuliwa chini ya jina linalokihusu — cha kwanza zawadi kutoka kwa rafiki, cha pili kilichopokezwa kupitia mnyororo mrefu wa wahubiri — ili uone kwamba hadithi ya kuazima haipotezi hata chembe ya nguvu zake pale kuazima kunapokubaliwa kwa sauti.
An illustration of Gerry Taillon — used by permission
Kielelezo cha Gerry Taillon — kinatumika kwa ruhusa

My father was a dentist, and I knew nothing whatever about farming, but I had a yard full of grass that would not stop growing. I had once tried to burn it off, and the fire spread and very nearly took the whole town with it, so I decided there had to be a better way. Two goats, I figured, would be just the thing.

Baba yangu alikuwa daktari wa meno, nami sikujua lolote kabisa kuhusu kilimo, lakini nilikuwa na uwanja uliojaa nyasi zisizoacha kukua. Niliwahi kujaribu kuzichoma, na moto ukaenea na karibu kuuteketeza mji mzima, kwa hiyo nikaamua lazima kuwe na njia bora zaidi. Mbuzi wawili, niliwaza, wangefaa kabisa.

I heard of two ladies in Pike Lake who kept goats, and I drove over to have a look. "I've got one for you right now," one of them said. I told her I wasn't really ready — I didn't know the first thing about goats — but she assured me there was nothing to it and I would have no trouble at all. So I bought it. I tried to load it into the bed of the truck; that did not go well, and I ended up with the goat riding in the front seat beside me. As I pulled away, the lady flagged me down. "One more thing — I took her kid away this morning, so she'll need milking tonight, and twice a day after that. But it's easy."

Nilisikia habari ya wanawake wawili huko Pike Lake waliofuga mbuzi, nikaendesha gari kwenda kuangalia. "Nina mmoja kwa ajili yako sasa hivi," mmoja wao akasema. Nikamwambia sikuwa tayari kweli — sikujua hata jambo la kwanza kuhusu mbuzi — lakini akanihakikishia kwamba si jambo gumu hata kidogo na sitapata shida yoyote. Basi nikamnunua. Nilijaribu kumpakia nyuma ya gari la mizigo; hilo halikwenda vizuri, na mwishowe mbuzi akasafiri kwenye kiti cha mbele kando yangu. Nilipoanza kuondoka, yule mwanamke akanipungia mkono nisimame. "Jambo moja zaidi — nimemwondoa mwanawe asubuhi hii, kwa hiyo atahitaji kukamuliwa usiku huu, na mara mbili kwa siku baada ya hapo. Lakini ni rahisi."

On the way home I stopped at the library and picked up a book, How to Raise Goats the Modern Way. At the house I set the goat on a bale of hay in the garage that would soon become the barn, propped the book open to a picture of a man milking, sat down on a box, slid a pail underneath, and went to work. I had never handled anything like this in my life. I squeezed the way you would shake a man's hand — and nothing happened. I squeezed again, and again — still nothing.

Njiani kurudi nyumbani nilisimama maktabani nikachukua kitabu, Jinsi ya Kufuga Mbuzi kwa Njia ya Kisasa. Nyumbani nilimweka mbuzi juu ya mzigo wa nyasi kavu ndani ya gereji ambayo hivi karibuni ingekuwa zizi, nikakifungua kitabu kwenye picha ya mtu akikamua, nikaketi juu ya sanduku, nikaweka ndoo chini, nikaanza kazi. Sikuwahi kushika kitu kama hiki maishani mwangu. Nilikamua kama unavyompa mtu mkono kumsalimu — na hakuna kilichotokea. Nikakamua tena, na tena — bado hakuna kitu.

Plainly I needed more information. I went back inside and read the chapter on milking. It said that milking is like squeezing a tube of used toothpaste: you start at the top and roll downward, closing off the top first so the milk cannot shoot back up. That had been my whole trouble — I had been squeezing in the middle and sending all the milk straight up. When I did it the book's way, it worked.

Ni wazi nilihitaji habari zaidi. Nilirudi ndani nikasoma sura inayohusu kukamua. Ilisema kukamua ni kama kubana mrija wa dawa ya meno uliokwisha kutumika: unaanza juu na kubana kuelekea chini, ukifunga juu kwanza ili maziwa yasiweze kurudi juu. Hilo ndilo lililokuwa tatizo langu lote — nilikuwa nikibana katikati na kuyarudisha maziwa yote moja kwa moja juu. Nilipofanya kwa njia ya kitabu, ilifanya kazi.

The point is simply this: you must do first things first. Real production comes one step at a time. That is exactly what the Lord meant in the parable of the talents — if we are faithful in a few things, He will set us over many.

Hoja ni hii tu: lazima ufanye mambo ya kwanza kwanza. Uzalishaji wa kweli huja hatua moja baada ya nyingine. Ndivyo hasa Bwana alivyomaanisha katika mfano wa talanta — tukiwa waaminifu katika machache, atatuweka juu ya mengi.
Told to Dr. Cook by Dr. Fish — from the account of Francis Dixon
Kilisimuliwa kwa Dkt. Cook na Dkt. Fish — kutoka katika simulizi la Francis Dixon

In England there was a Baptist pastor named Francis Dixon. In his church was a young man named Peter, who did a great deal of work around the church, and one day they asked him to give his testimony. He stood and said: "I was stationed with the Royal Navy in Sydney, Australia. I was walking down George Street one day when, out of nowhere, a little white-haired man stepped up to me. 'Excuse me, sir,' he said, 'I would like to ask you a question, and I hope you won't be offended. If you were to die today, where would you be in eternity? The Bible says it is either heaven or hell. Think about it — won't you, sir? That's all. God bless you. Toodle-oo.' And he was gone." Peter said the question came like an arrow shot from the bow of God, and it lodged in his heart. For six months he laboured under deep conviction, not knowing what to do, until at last, back in England, he sought out the one Christian friend he had — and that friend led him to Christ.

Huko Uingereza kulikuwa na mchungaji wa Kibaptisti aitwaye Francis Dixon. Katika kanisa lake kulikuwa na kijana mmoja aitwaye Peter, aliyefanya kazi nyingi kanisani, na siku moja wakamwomba atoe ushuhuda wake. Akasimama akasema: "Nilikuwa nimepangiwa kazi na Jeshi la Wanamaji la Uingereza huko Sydney, Australia. Siku moja nilikuwa nikitembea kwenye George Street wakati, ghafla tu, mzee mdogo mwenye nywele nyeupe alinijia. 'Samahani, bwana,' akasema, 'ningependa kukuuliza swali, natumaini hutaudhika. Kama ungekufa leo, ungekuwa wapi katika umilele? Biblia inasema ni mbinguni au jehanamu. Lifikirie — utalifikiria, bwana? Ni hayo tu. Mungu akubariki. Toodle-oo.' Kisha akatoweka." Peter alisema swali lile lilikuja kama mshale uliofyatuliwa kutoka katika upinde wa Mungu, ukakita moyoni mwake. Kwa miezi sita aliteseka chini ya kusadikishwa dhambi sana, bila kujua la kufanya, mpaka mwishowe, akiwa amerudi Uingereza, alimtafuta rafiki mmoja tu Mkristo aliyekuwa naye — na rafiki huyo akamwongoza kwa Kristo.

Not long after, the church held a series of special meetings, and on the team was a young man named Noel, who was asked to give his testimony. He stood and said, "I lived part of my life in the beautiful Australian city of Sydney. I was walking down George Street one day when, out of nowhere, a little white-haired man stepped up to me" — and he told the very same words, the same question, the same "Toodle-oo," the same vanishing. "I knew just enough of the gospel to be saved," Noel said, "and that very day I went back to my lodging, got down on my knees, and trusted Christ as my Savior." When the service ended, Peter came to him and said, "Noel, that is my testimony. The same little man came to me on George Street in Sydney."

Muda mfupi baadaye kanisa lilifanya mfululizo wa mikutano maalum, na katika timu kulikuwa na kijana aitwaye Noel, aliyeombwa atoe ushuhuda wake. Akasimama akasema, "Niliishi sehemu ya maisha yangu katika mji mzuri wa Australia wa Sydney. Siku moja nilikuwa nikitembea kwenye George Street wakati, ghafla tu, mzee mdogo mwenye nywele nyeupe alinijia" — naye akasimulia maneno yale yale, swali lile lile, "Toodle-oo" ile ile, kutoweka kule kule. "Nilijua injili kiasi cha kutosha tu kuokolewa," Noel akasema, "na siku ile ile nilirudi mahali nilipokuwa nikiishi, nikapiga magoti, nikamwamini Kristo kama Mwokozi wangu." Ibada ilipokwisha, Peter alimwendea akasema, "Noel, huo ndio ushuhuda wangu. Mzee yule yule mdogo alinijia mimi kwenye George Street huko Sydney."

The pastor overheard them. Not long after, preaching in Adelaide, he told the story of the two men in his church who had been led to the Lord by the little white-haired man of George Street. As he spoke, a man in the congregation began to wave his hand. "Sir," said Dixon, "did you wish to say something?" "Yes, I do," the man answered. "I want to tell you how I became a Christian. I was walking down George Street one day when, out of nowhere, a little white-haired man stepped up to me..." The story was the same.

Mchungaji aliwasikia. Muda mfupi baadaye, akihubiri huko Adelaide, alisimulia habari ya wanaume wawili katika kanisa lake walioongozwa kwa Bwana na yule mzee mdogo mwenye nywele nyeupe wa George Street. Alipokuwa akisema, mtu mmoja katika kusanyiko alianza kupunga mkono. "Bwana," Dixon akasema, "ulitaka kusema jambo?" "Ndiyo," mtu yule akajibu. "Nataka kukuambia jinsi nilivyokuwa Mkristo. Siku moja nilikuwa nikitembea kwenye George Street wakati, ghafla tu, mzee mdogo mwenye nywele nyeupe alinijia..." Hadithi ilikuwa ile ile.

Now Dixon knew he had something. He flew to Perth and told the story of the three men; at the close, a middle-aged Baptist deacon came to him: "Sir, I am another. I was walking down George Street..." The story was the same. Back in England he told it again, and a woman came: "Sir, I am another." At Keswick, at a convention on the deeper life, an aged man came: "Sir, I am another." In India, asked to preach on personal evangelism, he told it, and a missionary woman came: "Sir, I am another." On the voyage home, on the island of Jamaica, an eighth soul came: "Sir, I am another — a little man on George Street." And a layman telling the story in Fort Benning, Georgia, to a company of chaplains, heard one of them say, "Let me tell you how I became a Christian. I was walking down George Street one day..."

Sasa Dixon alijua kwamba alikuwa na jambo fulani. Alisafiri kwa ndege hadi Perth akasimulia habari ya wanaume wale watatu; mwishoni, shemasi wa Kibaptisti wa makamo alimjia: "Bwana, mimi ni mwingine. Nilikuwa nikitembea kwenye George Street..." Hadithi ilikuwa ile ile. Aliporudi Uingereza aliisimulia tena, na mwanamke mmoja akaja: "Bwana, mimi ni mwingine." Huko Keswick, katika mkutano mkuu juu ya maisha ya ndani zaidi ya kiroho, mzee mmoja akaja: "Bwana, mimi ni mwingine." Huko India, alipoombwa kuhubiri juu ya uinjilisti wa mtu kwa mtu, aliisimulia, na mwanamke mmishonari akaja: "Bwana, mimi ni mwingine." Katika safari ya kurudi nyumbani, katika kisiwa cha Jamaika, nafsi ya nane ikaja: "Bwana, mimi ni mwingine — mzee mdogo kwenye George Street." Na mlei mmoja aliyekuwa akisimulia habari hii huko Fort Benning, Georgia, kwa kundi la makasisi wa jeshi, alimsikia mmoja wao akisema, "Ngoja nikuambie jinsi nilivyokuwa Mkristo. Siku moja nilikuwa nikitembea kwenye George Street..."

By now Francis Dixon was determined to find the little white-haired man. He made certain that Sydney was on his next itinerary, and when he arrived he telephoned a Christian friend. "Do you know anything about a little white-haired man on George Street who asks people where they would be in eternity if they were to die?" "Certainly," came the voice. "That is Mr. Jenner. We all know him. He doesn't get out to the street much anymore — he is old now, and frail, and his sight is poor. But I could take you straight to his house."

Kufikia sasa Francis Dixon alikuwa ameazimia kumtafuta yule mzee mdogo mwenye nywele nyeupe. Alihakikisha kwamba Sydney imo katika ratiba ya safari yake iliyofuata, na alipofika alimpigia simu rafiki Mkristo. "Unajua lolote kuhusu mzee mdogo mwenye nywele nyeupe kwenye George Street anayewauliza watu wangekuwa wapi katika umilele kama wangekufa?" "Bila shaka," sauti ikajibu. "Huyo ni Bw. Jenner. Sote tunamjua. Siku hizi hatoki sana barabarani — amezeeka sasa, ni dhaifu, na macho yake hayaoni vizuri. Lakini ningeweza kukupeleka moja kwa moja nyumbani kwake."

So the two of them went to the home of the little old man, knocked, and were introduced. Francis Dixon told him of all the people, across the whole world, who had come to Christ through his pointed word of warning and witness. And the old man broke down and wept, and wept, and said: "Sir, I have shared the gospel with thousands of people on George Street in Sydney. This is the first time in all my life that I have ever heard of even one who came to Christ through my witness."

Basi wawili hao walikwenda nyumbani kwa yule mzee mdogo, wakabisha hodi, wakatambulishwa. Francis Dixon akamweleza habari ya watu wote, katika dunia nzima, waliokuja kwa Kristo kupitia neno lake kali la onyo na ushuhuda. Na yule mzee akavunjika moyo akalia, akalia, akasema: "Bwana, nimeishiriki injili na maelfu ya watu kwenye George Street huko Sydney. Hii ni mara ya kwanza katika maisha yangu yote kusikia habari ya hata mmoja aliyekuja kwa Kristo kupitia ushuhuda wangu."

Dr. Cook preaches that story where the Lord speaks of sowing and reaping — John 4, beside the well, where Jesus lifts the disciples' eyes to fields already white for harvest and tells them that one sows and another reaps, that He sends them to reap that for which they have not laboured. Mr. Jenner sowed for a lifetime and was given to reap nothing he could see; yet the harvest was real all the while, gathered into churches and missions and army camps on the far side of the earth. Here is the promise hidden in the heart of the illustration, and the reason it belongs to a sermon and not merely to a storybook: the faithful witness who labours and sees no fruit has not failed, for the God who keeps the account is bringing in a harvest he may not learn of until heaven. Tell it under Mr. Jenner's name, and it will preach.

Dkt. Cook huhubiri hadithi hiyo mahali ambapo Bwana anazungumza juu ya kupanda na kuvuna — Yohana 4, kando ya kisima, ambapo Yesu anayainua macho ya wanafunzi kuyaona mashamba yaliyokwisha kuwa meupe tayari kuvunwa na kuwaambia kwamba mmoja hupanda na mwingine huvuna, kwamba amewatuma wavune wasichokitaabikia. Bw. Jenner alipanda maisha yake yote wala hakupewa kuvuna chochote alichoweza kukiona; lakini mavuno yalikuwa halisi muda wote huo, yakikusanywa ndani ya makanisa na misheni na kambi za jeshi upande wa pili wa dunia. Hii hapa ahadi iliyofichwa moyoni mwa kielelezo, na sababu kinastahili kuwa sehemu ya mahubiri na si cha kitabu cha hadithi tu: shahidi mwaminifu anayetaabika bila kuona matunda hajashindwa, kwa maana Mungu anayeshika hesabu analeta mavuno ambayo shahidi huyo huenda asiyajue mpaka mbinguni. Isimulie chini ya jina la Bw. Jenner, nayo itahubiri.

Two further duties belong here. The first is truthfulness: a true story must stay true. You may tell it vividly, but you may not improve it into a lie — and if a story is hypothetical, you must say "suppose," and if it is a legend, you must not pass it off as fact. This is the very rule of Unit 4 ("thou shalt not add") carried from the text into the illustration: truth in the picture, as in the passage. The second is permission and privacy: when you illustrate from the lives of real people — a member of your congregation, your own family — get their permission, guard their dignity, change what should be changed, and never use the pulpit to expose or embarrass a soul who cannot answer back. The story serves the truth; it must never be allowed to wound the people the truth is meant to save.

Kuna wajibu mwingine miwili unaohusika hapa. Wa kwanza ni ukweli: hadithi ya kweli lazima ibaki ya kweli. Unaweza kuisimulia kwa uhai, lakini huwezi kuiboresha hadi iwe uongo — na kama hadithi ni ya kudhania, lazima useme "tuseme," na kama ni hekaya ya mapokeo, usiipitishe kana kwamba ni ukweli. Hii ndiyo kanuni ile ile ya Sehemu ya 4 ("usiongeze") ikihamishwa kutoka kifungu cha Maandiko kwenda kielelezo: ukweli katika picha, kama ulivyo katika kifungu. Wa pili ni ruhusa na faragha: unapotoa vielelezo kutoka maisha ya watu halisi — mshiriki wa kusanyiko lako, familia yako mwenyewe — pata ruhusa yao, linda heshima yao, badilisha kile kinachopaswa kubadilishwa, na kamwe usiitumie mimbari kumfichua au kumwaibisha mtu asiyeweza kujibu. Hadithi inatumikia kweli; kamwe isiruhusiwe kuwajeruhi watu ambao kweli inakusudia kuwaokoa.

There is a reason this matters more than mere good manners. We preach a gospel whose whole power is that it is true, and a man who lies in the small things of the pulpit teaches his people, without a word, that truth is negotiable when it serves the speaker. The borrowed story told as your own is a little parable of dishonesty preached alongside the sermon, and it undoes in the hearer's spirit what the text was building. The danger has only grown in an age when whole sermons can be downloaded and preached as one's own with a few clicks. The same rule covers them all: what you did not produce, you do not claim. Stand on your own study, tell borrowed stories under their owners' names, and let your integrity preach as loudly as your words.

Kuna sababu jambo hili ni muhimu kuliko adabu njema tu. Tunahubiri injili ambayo nguvu yake yote ni kwamba ni ya kweli, na mtu anayesema uongo katika mambo madogo ya mimbarini huwafundisha watu wake, bila neno, kwamba kweli inaweza kujadiliwa pale inapomfaa msemaji. Hadithi ya kuazima inayosimuliwa kama yako ni mfano mdogo wa kukosa uaminifu unaohubiriwa sambamba na mahubiri, nayo huvunja ndani ya roho ya msikilizaji kile ambacho kifungu kilikuwa kikijenga. Hatari hii imeongezeka tu katika zama ambazo mahubiri mazima yanaweza kupakuliwa na kuhubiriwa kama ya mtu mwenyewe kwa kubofya mara chache. Kanuni ile ile inayahusu yote: usichokitayarisha mwenyewe, usikidai. Simama juu ya masomo yako mwenyewe, simulia hadithi za kuazima chini ya majina ya wenyewe, na uache uadilifu wako uhubiri kwa sauti kubwa kama maneno yako.
7.5 Restraint
7.5 Kiasi

How many windows, then, should a sermon have? There is no fixed number, but a useful instinct is this: enough to light every main room, and no more. Each major point may well deserve its window; the minor turns can usually stand in the plain light of the others. Beware the two extremes — the windowless sermon that no one can see into, and the all-glass sermon that cannot bear its own weight. And place your illustrations where the light is most needed: at the hardest, most abstract point, where the hearer is straining to follow; at the moment of application, where the truth must move from the head to the hands; and at the close, where one last picture can send the people home carrying the whole message in a single image.

Basi mahubiri yanapaswa kuwa na madirisha mangapi? Hakuna idadi maalum, lakini hisia yenye manufaa ni hii: ya kutosha kuangaza kila chumba kikuu, wala si zaidi. Kila hoja kuu inaweza kustahili dirisha lake; mageuko madogo kwa kawaida yanaweza kusimama katika nuru ya kawaida ya mengine. Jihadhari na pande mbili za kupita kiasi — mahubiri yasiyo na madirisha ambayo hakuna anayeweza kuona ndani yake, na mahubiri ya kioo kitupu yasiyoweza kubeba uzito wake mwenyewe. Na weka vielelezo vyako mahali ambapo nuru inahitajika zaidi: kwenye hoja ngumu zaidi na dhahania zaidi, pale msikilizaji anapojikaza kufuata; wakati wa matumizi, pale kweli inapopaswa kuhama kutoka kichwani hadi mikononi; na mwishoni, pale picha moja ya mwisho inapoweza kuwarudisha watu nyumbani wakiubeba ujumbe wote katika picha moja.

One last principle holds all the rest in place. An illustration is a window, not the building — and a wall that is all windows will not stand. The preacher who loves stories must guard against letting them crowd out the very exposition they exist to serve, until the sermon is a charming string of anecdotes with a few verses scattered between. Light is good, but a house is more than light; the people came to hear the Word of God, not merely to be entertained by its preacher. Here is the test that exposes a misused illustration: if your hearers go home remembering the story but unable to recall the point it was meant to carry, then the window has become the view. The story drew all eyes to itself and let no light onto the truth. Keep every illustration in its place, a servant of the point and of the Word — used honestly, credited fairly, told truthfully, and held within bounds. Do that, and the small story inside the sermon will do its humble, shining work for as long as you preach. In the final unit we gather up the whole course into the craft of telling the story well, and put it to work in a closing workshop.

Kanuni moja ya mwisho inazishika nyingine zote mahali pake. Kielelezo ni dirisha, si jengo — na ukuta uliojaa madirisha tu hautasimama. Mhubiri anayependa hadithi lazima ajilinde asiziache zisonge nje ufafanuzi ule ule ambao zipo kuutumikia, hadi mahubiri yanakuwa mfululizo wa visa vya kupendeza na mistari michache iliyotawanyika katikati. Nuru ni nzuri, lakini nyumba ni zaidi ya nuru; watu walikuja kusikia Neno la Mungu, si kuburudishwa tu na mhubiri wake. Hiki hapa kipimo kinachofichua kielelezo kilichotumiwa vibaya: ikiwa wasikilizaji wako wanarudi nyumbani wakiikumbuka hadithi lakini hawawezi kukumbuka hoja iliyokusudiwa kubebwa nayo, basi dirisha limegeuka kuwa mandhari. Hadithi ilivuta macho yote kwake yenyewe na haikuacha nuru yoyote iangaze kweli. Weka kila kielelezo mahali pake, mtumishi wa hoja na wa Neno — kikitumiwa kwa uaminifu, chanzo chake kikitajwa kwa haki, kikisimuliwa kwa ukweli, na kikiwekwa ndani ya mipaka. Fanya hivyo, na hadithi ndogo ndani ya mahubiri itafanya kazi yake ya unyenyekevu na ya kung'aa kwa muda wote utakaohubiri. Katika sehemu ya mwisho tunaikusanya kozi nzima kuwa ufundi wa kusimulia hadithi vizuri, na kuitumia katika warsha ya kufunga.

Telling the Story Well — and a Workshop
Kuisimulia Simulizi Vizuri — na Warsha

We have learned why the story works, the three forms it may take, how to mine the Bible's own narratives, the craft of biographical preaching, the genius of the parables, and the honest use of the illustration. One thing remains — the telling itself. A great story badly told is a tragedy in the pulpit; the same story well told can turn a life around. This final unit takes up the craft of writing and telling, gathers the whole course into a handful of governing principles, and sends you out through a closing workshop.

Tumejifunza kwa nini simulizi hufanya kazi, maumbo matatu inayoweza kuchukua, jinsi ya kuchimba masimulizi ya Biblia yenyewe, ufundi wa kuhubiri maisha ya wahusika wa Biblia, ustadi wa ajabu wa mifano, na matumizi ya uaminifu ya kielelezo. Limebaki jambo moja — kusimulia kwenyewe. Simulizi kubwa iliyosimuliwa vibaya ni msiba mimbarini; simulizi ile ile ikisimuliwa vizuri inaweza kugeuza maisha ya mtu. Sehemu hii ya mwisho inashughulikia ufundi wa kuandika na kusimulia, inakusanya kozi nzima katika kanuni chache zinazotawala, na inakutuma nje kupitia warsha ya kufunga.
8.1 Writing the Story
8.1 Kuiandika Simulizi

Before a story is told, it is shaped, and shaping it is real work. Writers like Raymond Clubb and others who have studied the craft point us to a few enduring principles. The first is the telling detail: a story is not made vivid by piling on description but by choosing the few concrete, sensory details that make the scene leap to life — the smell of the fish, the dust on the road, the tremor in a voice. A flood of detail drowns a story; one perfect detail lights it. The second is economy: the deadliest enemy of any story is clutter, and the writer's chief labor is cutting — every word that does not serve must go, for what you leave out is as important as what you keep. The third is tension: a story lives on conflict and suspense, so begin near the action rather than far before it, build steadily toward the turn, and never give away the ending in advance. The fourth is point of view: decide whose eyes the hearer will look through — the detached narrator's, or, in the first person, the eyes of one who stood in the scene. And the fifth gathers up the rest — the single effect: a well-made story aims at one dominant impression, and every word in it should bend toward that one impression, so that the whole leaves a single, unforgettable mark.

Kabla simulizi haijasimuliwa, inaundwa, na kuiunda ni kazi halisi. Waandishi kama Raymond Clubb na wengine waliochunguza ufundi huu wanatuelekeza kwenye kanuni chache zinazodumu. Ya kwanza ni undani unaosema: simulizi haifanywi hai kwa kurundika maelezo, bali kwa kuchagua mambo machache halisi yanayogusa hisia, yanayofanya tukio liruke na kuwa hai — harufu ya samaki, vumbi barabarani, kutetemeka kwa sauti. Mafuriko ya maelezo huizamisha simulizi; undani mmoja mkamilifu huiwasha. Ya pili ni uchumi wa maneno: adui mkubwa kabisa wa simulizi yoyote ni msongamano, na kazi kuu ya mwandishi ni kukata — kila neno lisilotumikia lazima liondoke, kwa maana kile unachokiacha ni muhimu kama kile unachokibakiza. Ya tatu ni mvutano: simulizi huishi kwa mgogoro na hamu ya kujua kitakachotokea, kwa hiyo anza karibu na tukio lenyewe badala ya mbali kabla yake, jenga hatua kwa hatua kuelekea mgeuko, na kamwe usiufichue mwisho mapema. Ya nne ni mtazamo: amua msikilizaji atatazama kwa macho ya nani — ya msimulizi aliye nje ya tukio, au, kwa nafsi ya kwanza, macho ya mtu aliyesimama ndani ya tukio. Na ya tano inakusanya zilizobaki — athari moja: simulizi iliyoundwa vizuri inalenga taswira moja kuu, na kila neno ndani yake linapaswa kuelekea taswira hiyo moja, ili jumla yake iache alama moja isiyosahaulika.

Two places in a story carry more weight than all the rest, and both deserve special labor: the first sentence and the last. The opening must seize attention before the hearer's mind can wander — not with throat-clearing ("I want to tell you a little story about...") but by dropping the hearer straight into the scene, in the middle of something happening. The close must land the single effect and then stop. The commonest fault of beginning storytellers is not knowing when the story is over, so they explain it, and re-explain it, and talk the life out of it. When the sting has struck, when the picture is complete, fall silent and trust the story you have told. A tale that ends one beat too late loses in its final seconds everything the preceding minutes had won.

Sehemu mbili za simulizi zina uzito kuliko nyingine zote, na zote mbili zinastahili juhudi ya pekee: sentensi ya kwanza na ya mwisho. Mwanzo lazima ukamate usikivu kabla akili ya msikilizaji haijaanza kutangatanga — si kwa kujisafisha koo ("Nataka kuwasimulia hadithi ndogo kuhusu..."), bali kwa kumtumbukiza msikilizaji moja kwa moja ndani ya tukio, katikati ya jambo linalotendeka. Mwisho lazima utue athari ile moja kisha ukomee hapo. Kosa la kawaida zaidi la wasimulizi wanaoanza ni kutojua simulizi inapokwisha, kwa hiyo wanaieleza, na kuieleza tena, na kuiondolea uhai kwa maneno mengi. Mchomo ukishapiga, picha ikishakamilika, nyamaza na uiamini simulizi uliyoisimulia. Hadithi inayoisha pigo moja kuchelewa hupoteza katika sekunde zake za mwisho kila kitu ambacho dakika zilizotangulia zilikuwa zimekipata.
8.2 Telling the Story
8.2 Kuisimulia Simulizi

A story that has been well written must still be well told, and telling is a different art from writing. The first rule is the hardest for many: a story in the pulpit is told, not read. A story read from a manuscript is half dead — the eyes drop to the page, the spontaneity drains away, and the hearer feels he is being recited to rather than spoken with. Know your story so thoroughly that you need no notes, and then you are free to look your people in the eye while you tell it. The second is pacing: a told story breathes, hurrying through what is minor, slowing at the turning point, and — most neglected of all — daring to fall silent at the great moment, for a well-placed pause can strike harder than any word. The third is that the teller's whole instrument is himself — his voice rising and falling, his face, his hands, the lean of his body — all enlisted, never to show off, but to carry the scene. The fourth is the secret of all vivid telling: see it as you tell it. If you yourself are watching the prodigal stumble up the road as you speak, your hearers will watch him too; if you see nothing, they will see nothing. And the fifth is the line that must never be crossed — feel it without performing it. Genuine feeling moves people; theatrics repel them, because the instant a congregation senses an act, the spell breaks and the trust with it. Tell it from the heart, and let the heart, not the performance, do the work.

Simulizi iliyoandikwa vizuri lazima bado isimuliwe vizuri, na kusimulia ni sanaa tofauti na kuandika. Kanuni ya kwanza ndiyo ngumu zaidi kwa wengi: simulizi mimbarini husimuliwa, haisomwi. Simulizi inayosomwa kutoka kwenye muswada ni nusu mfu — macho yanashuka kwenye ukurasa, uchangamfu wa papo hapo unatoweka, na msikilizaji anahisi kwamba anasomewa badala ya kuzungumzwa naye. Ijue simulizi yako kikamilifu kiasi kwamba huhitaji maandishi yoyote, na hapo utakuwa huru kuwatazama watu wako machoni unapoisimulia. Ya pili ni mwendo: simulizi inayosimuliwa hupumua, ikiharakisha mambo madogo, ikipunguza mwendo kwenye mgeuko, na — jambo linalosahaulika kuliko yote — ikithubutu kunyamaza katika wakati mkuu, kwa maana kimya kilichowekwa mahali pake kinaweza kupiga kwa nguvu kuliko neno lolote. Ya tatu ni kwamba chombo kizima cha msimulizi ni yeye mwenyewe — sauti yake ikipanda na kushuka, uso wake, mikono yake, mwinamo wa mwili wake — vyote vikitumika, kamwe si kwa kujionyesha, bali kulibeba tukio. Ya nne ndiyo siri ya kusimulia kote kulikojaa uhai: liona tukio unapolisimulia. Kama wewe mwenyewe unamtazama mwana mpotevu akijikokota barabarani unaponena, wasikilizaji wako nao watamtazama; usipoona chochote, wao hawataona chochote. Na ya tano ni mstari ambao kamwe usivukwe — ihisi bila kuiigiza. Hisia za kweli huwagusa watu; maigizo huwafukuza, kwa sababu mara tu kusanyiko linapohisi kuna uigizaji, uchawi wa simulizi unavunjika na uaminifu pamoja nao. Isimulie kutoka moyoni, na moyo, wala si maigizo, ufanye kazi.

How do you reach the point of telling a story without notes? By rehearsal, which is no shame but the storyteller's ordinary discipline. Tell it aloud to the empty room, to the steering wheel of your car, to anyone who will listen, until the shape of it lives in you and the words come of themselves. Do not memorize it word for word as a speech to be recited — a memorized story is as stiff as a read one, and the moment you forget a phrase you are lost. Memorize instead the sequence of pictures, the scenes in their order, and let the words be born fresh each time you tell it. A story known this way can be told to a child at bedtime or to a congregation on Sunday with equal ease, because it is no longer on a page; it is in you.

Unafikaje mahali pa kusimulia simulizi bila maandishi? Kwa mazoezi ya kurudiarudia, ambayo si aibu bali ni nidhamu ya kawaida ya msimulizi. Isimulie kwa sauti katika chumba kitupu, kwa usukani wa gari lako, kwa mtu yeyote atakayesikiliza, mpaka umbo lake liishi ndani yako na maneno yaje yenyewe. Usiikariri neno kwa neno kama hotuba ya kughani — simulizi iliyokaririwa ni ngumu kama iliyosomwa, na mara unaposahau kifungu kimoja cha maneno umepotea. Badala yake kariri mfuatano wa picha, matukio kwa mpangilio wake, na uyaache maneno yazaliwe upya kila mara unapoisimulia. Simulizi inayojulikana kwa njia hii inaweza kusimuliwa kwa mtoto wakati wa kulala au kwa kusanyiko siku ya Jumapili kwa urahisi ule ule, kwa sababu haiko tena kwenye ukurasa; iko ndani yako.
8.3 The Marks of a Good Storyteller
8.3 Alama za Msimulizi Mzuri

Several teachers of preaching, among them Martin Thielen and Robert Hastings, have set down lists of the marks that distinguish the effective storyteller, and the serious student will want to read them for himself. The marks they describe gather around a few simple instincts that bear repeating in our own words. The good storyteller keeps it short and keeps it moving, trusting the story rather than padding it. He deals in the concrete and the specific, not the vague and the general, because the soul sees pictures, not abstractions. He tells with warmth and conviction, as a man who believes what he is saying and cares that you hear it. He aims past the ear at the heart, where decisions are actually made. And through it all he keeps himself out of the way, so that the hearer remembers the truth and the Lord, not the cleverness of the man in the pulpit. None of this is a trick to be performed; it is the natural shape of love speaking truth through a story.

Walimu kadhaa wa kuhubiri, miongoni mwao Martin Thielen na Robert Hastings, wameandika orodha za alama zinazomtofautisha msimulizi mwenye ufanisi, na mwanafunzi makini atataka kuzisoma mwenyewe. Alama wanazozieleza zinakusanyika kuzunguka silika chache rahisi zinazostahili kurudiwa kwa maneno yetu wenyewe. Msimulizi mzuri huifanya fupi na kuifanya isonge mbele, akiiamini simulizi badala ya kuijaza maneno yasiyo ya lazima. Hushughulika na mambo halisi na mahususi, si ya jumla na yasiyo wazi, kwa sababu nafsi huona picha, si dhana tupu. Husimulia kwa uchangamfu na usadikisho, kama mtu anayeamini anachokisema na anayejali kwamba umsikie. Hulenga kupita sikio hadi moyoni, mahali maamuzi hufanyika kwa kweli. Na katika yote hayo hujiweka kando, ili msikilizaji akumbuke kweli na Bwana, si werevu wa mtu aliye mimbarini. Hakuna lolote kati ya haya lililo hila ya kuigizwa; ni umbo la asili la upendo unaonena kweli kupitia simulizi.

Take heart if you do not think of yourself as a natural storyteller. A few are born with the gift, but most good preachers were made, not born — they learned to see, learned to cut, learned to slow down at the turn, learned by telling a hundred stories badly before they told one well. The marks described above are not a personality you either have or lack; they are habits any earnest preacher can cultivate over years. Watch how the people you most love to listen to do it. Notice what makes a story land and what makes it fall flat. Keep telling, keep failing, keep learning. The pulpit is not reserved for the naturally gifted; it is open to the faithful who will do the work, and the Lord who gave the parables delights to teach a willing man to tell them.

Jipe moyo ikiwa hujioni kuwa msimulizi wa kuzaliwa. Wachache huzaliwa na kipawa hicho, lakini wahubiri wengi wazuri walifanywa, hawakuzaliwa hivyo — walijifunza kuona, walijifunza kukata, walijifunza kupunguza mwendo kwenye mgeuko, walijifunza kwa kusimulia simulizi mia moja vibaya kabla hawajasimulia moja vizuri. Alama zilizoelezwa hapo juu si tabia ya kuzaliwa ambayo ama unayo ama huna; ni mazoea ambayo mhubiri yeyote mwenye bidii anaweza kuyakuza kwa miaka. Tazama jinsi watu unaopenda zaidi kuwasikiliza wanavyofanya. Angalia kinachofanya simulizi ifike na kinachoifanya ianguke bure. Endelea kusimulia, endelea kukosea, endelea kujifunza. Mimbari haikuwekwa kwa wenye vipawa vya asili peke yao; iko wazi kwa waaminifu watakaofanya kazi, na Bwana aliyetoa mifano hufurahi kumfundisha mtu aliye tayari jinsi ya kuisimulia.
8.4 The Whole Course in One Hand
8.4 Kozi Nzima Katika Mkono Mmoja

Gather the eight units now into principles you can carry in one hand. First, the story is a worthy vessel for the Word of God, not a compromise, for the Lord Himself made it His chief method (Unit 1). Second, preach to the whole person, satisfying the mind and seizing the heart (Unit 2). Third, choose the form the message requires — deductive, inductive, or controlling story — letting the form serve the truth and never the reverse (Unit 3). Fourth through sixth, the Bible's own narratives, the lives of its people, and the parables of Jesus are your richest material; study them deeply, retell them vividly, and never add to or contradict the text (Units 4-6). Seventh, the small story inside the sermon is a window, to be used honestly, credited fairly, and held within bounds (Unit 7). And eighth, tell it well and tell it true (this unit). Over all of these stands the one principle that has governed the course from the first page: the story is always a servant — of the truth, and of the hearer's meeting with God. The moment it becomes an end in itself, a display of the preacher's gifts, it has betrayed its calling. Keep it a servant, and it will do in your ministry what it did in the ministry of the Lord who told the greatest stories ever heard.

Sasa kusanya sehemu hizi nane kuwa kanuni unazoweza kuzibeba katika mkono mmoja. Kwanza, simulizi ni chombo kinachostahili kubeba Neno la Mungu, si maafikiano, kwa maana Bwana Mwenyewe aliifanya kuwa njia yake kuu (Sehemu ya 1). Pili, mhubirie mtu mzima, ukiitosheleza akili na kuukamata moyo (Sehemu ya 2). Tatu, chagua umbo ambalo ujumbe unalihitaji — la kideduktivu, la kiinduktivu, au simulizi inayotawala — ukiacha umbo litumikie kweli na kamwe si kinyume chake (Sehemu ya 3). Nne hadi sita, masimulizi ya Biblia yenyewe, maisha ya watu wake, na mifano ya Yesu ndiyo malighafi yako tajiri zaidi; yachunguze kwa kina, yasimulie upya kwa uhai, na kamwe usiongeze juu ya kifungu wala kukipinga (Sehemu ya 4-6). Saba, simulizi ndogo ndani ya mahubiri ni dirisha, la kutumiwa kwa uaminifu, kutajiwa chanzo chake kwa haki, na kuwekewa mipaka (Sehemu ya 7). Na nane, isimulie vizuri na isimulie kwa kweli (sehemu hii). Juu ya yote haya inasimama kanuni moja ambayo imeitawala kozi tangu ukurasa wa kwanza: simulizi daima ni mtumishi — wa kweli, na wa kukutana kwa msikilizaji na Mungu. Mara inapogeuka kuwa lengo lenyewe, onyesho la vipawa vya mhubiri, imeusaliti wito wake. Iweke iwe mtumishi, nayo itafanya katika huduma yako kile ilichofanya katika huduma ya Bwana aliyesimulia simulizi kuu kuliko zote zilizowahi kusikika.
8.5 A Worked Capstone and Your Workshop
8.5 Mfano wa Kazi wa Kufunga na Warsha Yako

See it all in one sermon. Dr. Cook's message "The Backside of God" is built on Exodus 33, where Moses dares to ask, "Shew me thy glory," and the LORD answers that no man can see His face and live — yet places Moses in the cleft of the rock, covers him with His hand, and lets him see His "back parts" as the glory passes by. Here is the disciplined study of a narrative (Unit 4), and out of it rises a single controlling image (Unit 3): the backside of God — for what we are given to see of God in this life is not His face but His afterward, the trail of glory He leaves where He has already passed. The truth is then contemporized (Unit 4) and carried near with a vivid modern picture, the great river running through the Alberta valley, so that a congregation far from Sinai feels the wonder for themselves. And the whole sermon lands one unforgettable truth: we cannot see the face of God now, but we can always see where He has been — and to have seen where God has passed is enough to trust Him with the road ahead. Study, form, controlling image, contemporizing, faithful retelling, one clear truth — the whole course, standing in a single sermon.

Liona jambo lote katika mahubiri mamoja. Ujumbe wa Dkt. Cook "Upande wa Nyuma wa Mungu" umejengwa juu ya Kutoka 33, ambapo Musa anathubutu kuomba, "Unionyeshe utukufu wako," naye BWANA anajibu kwamba hakuna binadamu atakayeuona uso wake akaishi — lakini anamweka Musa katika ufa wa mwamba, anamfunika kwa mkono wake, na kumwacha aone "nyuma yake" utukufu unapopita. Hapa kuna uchunguzi wenye nidhamu wa simulizi (Sehemu ya 4), na kutoka humo inainuka picha moja inayotawala (Sehemu ya 3): upande wa nyuma wa Mungu — kwa maana kile tunachopewa kuona cha Mungu katika maisha haya si uso wake bali alama anazoacha baada ya kupita, njia ya utukufu anayoiacha mahali ambapo amekwisha kupita. Kisha kweli hiyo inaletwa katika wakati wa sasa (Sehemu ya 4) na kusogezwa karibu kwa picha ya kisasa iliyo hai, mto mkubwa unaopita katika bonde la Alberta, ili kusanyiko lililo mbali na Sinai lihisi mshangao huo wao wenyewe. Na mahubiri yote yanatua kwenye kweli moja isiyosahaulika: hatuwezi kuuona uso wa Mungu sasa, lakini daima tunaweza kuona mahali alipopita — na kuona mahali Mungu alipopita kunatosha kumwamini kwa ajili ya njia iliyo mbele. Uchunguzi, umbo, picha inayotawala, kuileta kweli katika wakati wa sasa, kusimulia upya kwa uaminifu, kweli moja iliyo wazi — kozi nzima, ikisimama katika mahubiri mamoja.

Now the work passes to you. Your workshop is not a paragraph to read but a sermon to build. Take a biblical narrative that grips you. Study it through the five windows of Unit 4 until you see the scene clearly. Choose the form it needs — will you state the point and illustrate it, withhold the point and let them discover it, or let one story govern the whole? Find the controlling image or follow the arc; write the story with the craft of detail, economy, tension, point of view, and single effect; and then put down your notes and tell it aloud, again and again, until you can see it and feel it without the page. Those preparing written work for the Th.M. or M.Div. should set the finished narrative sermon down in full. And when it is built, preach it — honestly, faithfully, and well. You came to learn how to preach with a story; go now and do it, so that through the truth you tell, men and women may meet the living God. This is the end of the course, and the beginning of your storytelling.

Sasa kazi inakabidhiwa kwako. Warsha yako si aya ya kusoma bali ni mahubiri ya kujenga. Chukua simulizi ya Kibiblia inayokukamata. Ichunguze kupitia madirisha matano ya Sehemu ya 4 mpaka ulione tukio waziwazi. Chagua umbo linalohitajika — je, utaitaja hoja kisha uieleze kwa kielelezo, utaizuia hoja na kuwaacha waigundue wenyewe, au utaacha simulizi moja itawale yote? Tafuta picha inayotawala au fuata msuko wa hadithi; iandike simulizi kwa ufundi wa undani, uchumi wa maneno, mvutano, mtazamo, na athari moja; kisha weka chini maandishi yako na uisimulie kwa sauti, tena na tena, mpaka uweze kuiona na kuihisi bila ukurasa. Wale wanaoandaa kazi ya maandishi kwa ajili ya Shahada ya Uzamili ya Teolojia (Th.M.) au Shahada ya Uzamili ya Huduma ya Kiungu (M.Div.) wanapaswa kuandika mahubiri kamili ya simulizi yaliyokamilika. Na yakishajengwa, yahubiri — kwa uaminifu, kwa kushika kweli, na vizuri. Ulikuja kujifunza jinsi ya kuhubiri kwa simulizi; sasa nenda ukafanye hivyo, ili kupitia kweli unayoisimulia, wanaume na wanawake wakutane na Mungu aliye hai. Huu ndio mwisho wa kozi, na mwanzo wa usimulizi wako.

And one word remains, the most important in the course. All the craft of these eight units — the forms, the study, the imagination, the telling — is worth nothing without the Spirit of God, who alone can take a story off your lips and drive it into a heart you could never reach. The greatest storyteller may move an audience to tears and never move a soul to Christ if he preaches in his own strength. So learn the craft with all diligence, and then kneel and ask the One who told the parables to breathe upon your telling. Prepare as if everything depended on your work; preach as if everything depended on His. Do both, and your stories will not merely be admired and remembered — they will become, in His hands, the very road by which a lost man walks home to God. Go, and tell it well.

Na limebaki neno moja, lililo muhimu kuliko yote katika kozi hii. Ufundi wote wa sehemu hizi nane — maumbo, uchunguzi, mawazo ya ubunifu, usimulizi — hauna thamani yoyote bila Roho wa Mungu, ambaye peke yake anaweza kuichukua simulizi kutoka midomoni mwako na kuisukuma ndani ya moyo ambao wewe kamwe usingeweza kuufikia. Msimulizi mkuu kabisa anaweza kuwatoa wasikilizaji machozi na bado asimsogeze hata nafsi moja kwa Kristo ikiwa anahubiri kwa nguvu zake mwenyewe. Kwa hiyo jifunze ufundi kwa bidii yote, kisha piga magoti umwombe Yule aliyesimulia mifano apulizie usimulizi wako. Jiandae kana kwamba kila kitu kinategemea kazi yako; hubiri kana kwamba kila kitu kinategemea kazi yake. Fanya yote mawili, na simulizi zako hazitapendezwa na kukumbukwa tu — zitakuwa, mikononi mwake, njia yenyewe ambayo kwayo mtu aliyepotea anarudi nyumbani kwa Mungu. Nenda, ukaisimulie vizuri.
